title: Providers, model catalogs and authentication
introduction: Source-derived comparison of provider identity, authentication, OAuth, model configuration and catalog lifecycle in the frozen TypeScript and Rust checkouts. The area contains 33 reviewed entries and reconciles 124 assigned files. Generic native provider packages, private execution bindings, auth commands and Faux support are credited. Exact redactions and external-package limitations remain explicit; no application, test or network request was executed.

entries.title: Credential schema, OAuth expiry units and provider metadata
entries.source:
ice:packages/ai/src/auth/types.ts:7-43; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts:119-178; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:305-310; source-read assertions ice:packages/ai/test/oauth-auth.test.ts:50-72 and ice:packages/ai/test/oauth-auth.test.ts:121-157.

Exported symbols: `CredentialInfo` (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/types.ts:40).
entries.what: Preserve a provider's complete login state and interpret token lifetime correctly when reading, refreshing or migrating credentials.
entries.mechanism:
Credentials are stored under a provider identity and retain the information that provider needs for later requests. OAuth expiry units and extra provider metadata must survive imports, refreshes and rewrites.

A credential is keyed by Provider.id, with one type-tagged value per provider. ApiKeyCredential is {type:"api_key", key?:string, env?:ProviderEnv}; OAuthCredential is {type:"oauth", refresh:string, access:string, expires:number,[key:string]:unknown}. ModelAuth is separate request data {apiKey?:string, headers?:ProviderHeaders, baseUrl?:string}; provider env/config may accompany AuthResult but is not an arbitrary OAuth token replacement (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/types.ts:7-37; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/types.ts:103-115).

OAuth expiry is compared directly with Date.now(), so it is an epoch-millisecond timestamp. A token expiring at or before now plus the minimum validity is eligible for refresh. Extra fields are material: GitHub Copilot's enterpriseUrl influences the request baseUrl, and refresh must preserve it. The coding AuthStorage parses JSON without stripping extra fields or validating the union at runtime, then replaces only the selected provider's value while retaining unrelated providers. ModelAuth.toAuth can produce a per-credential endpoint as well as a key (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts:135-178; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:305-310; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:361-382; ice:packages/ai/test/oauth-auth.test.ts:50-72; ice:packages/ai/test/oauth-auth.test.ts:93-117).

readStoredCredential is a separate best-effort, synchronous raw read: it neither resolves configured key expressions nor refreshes OAuth and returns undefined for any read/parse error (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:404-418).
entries.interfaces: CredentialStore.read(providerId,{signal?})→Promise<Credential|undefined>; list→non-secret {providerId, type}[]; modify(providerId, async current→next|undefined,{signal?}) returns the post-write credential, with undefined meaning unchanged, not deletion; delete is the only remove operation. The JSON root is Record<providerId, Credential>. OAuth.expires uses milliseconds; request ModelAuth may include headers and baseUrl.
entries.dependency_text: Provider-specific OAuth flows in AUTH-015 through AUTH-022 depend on preserving opaque credential fields. No external service is needed to read or store the format.
entries.rust: Rust has real provider-keyed credential storage, but Credential::Oauth has only access, refresh and expires:i64, whose documented and consumed units are epoch seconds; expires=0 means no known expiry and is treated as valid by credentials::resolve. The enum does not retain arbitrary OAuth metadata when parsed and rewritten. Thus directly copying a TS expires value makes it appear far in the future, and a subsequent native rewrite drops fields such as enterpriseUrl. Rust auth CLI accepts extension credentials in expires_at seconds and stores the fixed enum, rather than retaining a typed provider-specific bag (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:232-322; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/credentials.rs:71-90; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/auth.rs:169-209; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/auth.rs:297-313).
entries.port: Add an explicit compatibility conversion at import/read boundaries, with a documented source format and unit conversion rather than guessing that every large integer is milliseconds. Preserve provider-owned OAuth metadata through load, locked refresh and rewrite, preferably with a flattened JSON map or typed provider payload. Keep native seconds semantics available to existing extension action responses. Exercise source-specified cases in implementation work: TS millisecond expiry, native expires=0, permanent OpenRouter-style credentials, Copilot enterpriseUrl and unrelated provider entries. This audit did not read or modify any real auth.json.
entries.priority_reason: Incorrect expiry units and discarded metadata can make imported OAuth credentials silently unusable or prevent timely refresh.

entries.source:
ice:packages/ai/src/auth/credential-store.ts:1-68; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:34-230; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:233-267; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:361-394; source-read tests ice:packages/coding-agent/test/auth-storage.test.ts:105-299 and ice:packages/coding-agent/test/auth-storage.test.ts:327-423.

entries.what: Prevent concurrent logins, refreshes and logouts from losing updates, and ensure a cancelled operation cannot later overwrite credentials.
entries.mechanism:
Credential updates hold one owner across reading, changing and publishing the latest stored value. Cancellation prevents a late commit while active work retains ownership until it settles.

Every public credential mutation uses a serialized read/modify/write callback over the latest stored value. The generic in-memory store chains operations per provider; coding AuthStorage's in-memory backend serializes across all providers because it rewrites one JSON root. Callback failure leaves the entry unchanged; returning undefined also leaves it unchanged, and an explicit delete serializes against modifications (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/credential-store.ts:13-66; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:233-267; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:361-394).

The file backend creates a missing parent with mode 0700 and a missing auth.json with mode 0600, then acquires proper-lockfile ownership with realpath:false. Its synchronous path retries ELOCKED at most ten total attempts, busy-waiting 20 ms between attempts. The asynchronous path makes at most eleven attempts (attempts 0 through 10), disables library retries, sets stale:30000, and retries only ELOCKED with delay min(round((random()+1)*100*2^attempt),10000) ms. Abort is checked before creating anything, before each attempt and immediately after acquisition; a concurrently cancelled acquisition releases ownership before throwing (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:94-218).

The async backend tracks onCompromised, checks compromise and cancellation before callback, after callback and around the write, and retains the lock until an active callback settles even if the caller has cancelled. No late cancelled result is committed. Unlock errors are swallowed by the async finally block; the synchronous finally directly invokes release. File replacement follows an existing symlink to its real target, writes a PID plus four-random-byte temporary sibling with mode 0600, then renames; failure calls rmSync(force:true) on the temporary file before rethrowing. Cleanup failure is not caught separately and can replace the original write/rename error. The TS helper does not fsync the staging file or directory. A parse/callback/lock failure never intentionally rewrites malformed or stale content (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:52-66; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:135-150; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:189-230; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/auth-storage.test.ts:172-299; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/auth-storage.test.ts:480-486).

Generic in-memory enqueue races the returned promise against abort but keeps the internal chain until active work settles. It checks abort again before committing; cancellation of a queued task prevents that callback from running later. The coding in-memory backend applies the same commit/chain discipline across the shared JSON value (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/credential-store.ts:14-55; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:249-265).

Missing-file creation occurs before acquiring the file lock, using existsSync followed by ordinary writeFileSync rather than exclusive creation. The random temporary file also uses the same ordinary writer. Preserve the native writer's exclusive staging while adding the required cross-process transaction; initialization should not weaken its ownership guarantees (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:34-65; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:94-105).
entries.interfaces:
AuthStorageBackend.read():string|undefined; withLock(fn):T; withLockAsync(async fn,{signal?}):Promise<T>, where callback returns {result:T, next?:string}. next undefined means no file rewrite. Public CredentialStore.modify/delete expose optional AbortSignal; file locking is whole-file even though logical credentials are per provider.

`AuthOperationOptions` is exactly `{ signal?: AbortSignal }`; it is the optional cancellation input shared by public credential reads, listings and serialized mutation operations (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/types.ts:45-48).
entries.dependency_text: TS uses proper-lockfile, node fs and crypto. Rust target is the CLI credential repository; use an async ownership gate and an appropriate existing or explicitly added cross-process file-lock primitive.
entries.rust: Rust upsert_credential and delete_credential call read_auth, mutate a BTreeMap and write_auth without a lock, so concurrent updates can overwrite each other. Config source explicitly acknowledges this behavior. Native atomic_write already creates a unique sibling with create_new and mode 0600, writes and sync_all's it, closes and renames, removing the staging file on write/sync/rename failure; preserve these stronger staging guarantees. It renames over the supplied path rather than resolving a symlink target. Native methods are synchronous and have no abort-aware callback ownership or double-checked refresh transaction (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:20-26; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:272-337; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:981-1047).
entries.port: Implement a credential repository that holds cross-process ownership across authoritative reread, async refresh/login callback and commit. Do not release its gate merely because the awaiting caller aborts; cancel before starting queued work and suppress a cancelled result after active work settles. Preserve create_new, sync_all and failure cleanup, add explicit symlink-target policy, and keep existing private permissions. Reproduce the specified contention, logout-during-refresh, lock-compromise, cancelled-waiter and malformed-file cases during implementation; no tests were written or run in this audit.
entries.priority_reason: Token rotation and concurrent credential operations need a single commit owner to avoid lost or resurrected credentials.

entries.title: Credential read snapshots, error modes and secret-free enumeration
entries.what: Read changed credentials promptly without waiting for writers, keep status listings free of secret resolution side effects, and expose storage failures only in the intended call modes.
entries.mechanism:
Credential reads use a revision-aware snapshot so readers do not wait for a writer’s lock. Metadata listing avoids secret resolution, while explicit request reads have their own error and cancellation behavior.

AuthStorage reads outside the write lock because writers replace complete file contents. It caches the last parsed JSON plus a revision of dev:ino:size:mtimeNs:ctimeNs obtained with bigint stat; a matching defined revision returns the cached snapshot. A module-level slot shares a readState between newly constructed stores for the same most-recent normalized path, while instances retain their own reference after another path replaces that slot (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:36-49; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:272-287; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:328-350).

The revision is sampled before file content, making a concurrent later change trigger another reload. reload() always catches read/parse errors and preserves the last valid snapshot. read/list without a signal similarly fall back to the last snapshot if reload fails; when a signal argument exists they call reloadFromStorage without that catch, so storage/parse failure propagates, and pre-aborted operations reject. Missing files return undefined content, which parses as an empty root and clears the cached view rather than preserving disappeared credentials (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:85-91; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:305-359).

read(provider) returns OAuth unchanged. For API-key credentials with a defined key it resolves the configured key using credential.env and returns a copied credential with that key. list emits only {providerId, type}, retaining JS object enumeration order and never resolving API-key expressions; the generic in-memory store similarly lists Map insertion order. readStoredCredential is a synchronous raw read returning undefined on any error and is deliberately distinct from read's resolved-key contract (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:353-359; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-storage.ts:396-418; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/credential-store.ts:30-38).

The read tests assert changed-file propagation between stores without acquiring lockfile, immediate reading while another writer owns the file lock, scoped environment precedence, command-backed key resolution and pre-abort behavior. They were read as source, not executed (ice:packages/coding-agent/test/auth-storage.test.ts:28-103; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/auth-storage.test.ts:302-325).
entries.interfaces: AuthStorage.create(authPath?), fromStorage(backend), inMemory(initial={}), reload(), read(), list(), modify(), delete(); FileAuthStorageBackend default path is getAgentDir()/auth.json after normalizePath. Enumeration returns metadata only; request-time read may resolve a configured key expression. Exact expression expansion is owned by the settings/config-value entry.
entries.dependency_text: SET-005 owns environment templates and strict/lenient headers; SET-006 owns command execution/cache, timeout and failure caching. AuthStorage owns when those resolvers are invoked; no network request is required for metadata enumeration.
entries.rust: Rust read_auth rereads and fully deserializes the file on every call, returns an empty BTreeMap for a missing file, and propagates malformed JSON or I/O errors with ConfigError. It has no revision snapshot, shared read-state cache or optional-signal-dependent fallback. Native auth check calls credentials::resolve, which resolves stored/configured key expressions, and only then reports a non-secret source; that is not a CredentialStore.list equivalent, even though it avoids printing token material (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:143-167; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:258-269; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/credentials.rs:57-126; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/auth.rs:367-394).
entries.port: Add metadata-only enumeration and distinguish raw persisted credentials, resolved request credentials, and local readiness checks in the CLI repository API. Implement revision-aware lock-free reads if matching the coding SDK contract, with the exact failure/cancellation branches above rather than an unconditional stale-data fallback. Keep strict raw read available as a native mode. Source listings and UI status must not invoke configured secret commands unless the specific request-auth/check path authorizes that behavior.
entries.priority_reason: Credential changes and status checks need predictable freshness and side effects across concurrent sessions.

entries.source:
ice:packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts:1-206; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/helpers.ts:9-30; source-read tests ice:packages/ai/test/models-runtime.test.ts:617-1074 and ice:packages/coding-agent/test/auth-storage.test.ts:425-478.

Exported symbols: `envApiKeyAuth` (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/helpers.ts:9).
Exported symbols: `ModelsErrorCode` (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts:16).
entries.what: Resolve the selected provider's credentials for a request, refresh near-expiry OAuth once under ownership, and preserve meaningful cancellation and failure results.
entries.mechanism:
Each request resolves authentication for its selected provider before execution. Stored credentials remain authoritative, and near-expiry OAuth tokens are rechecked and refreshed under credential-store ownership.

resolveProviderAuth creates a concrete operation signal and races its public result against that caller signal. It first overlays request env values onto AuthContext using env[name] || base.env(name), so empty overrides do not mask ambient values. If apiKey is explicitly supplied and the provider has an API-key handler, that handler receives a synthetic API-key credential with the supplied key/env before any stored credential is read. An empty string still enters this override branch; the handler decides whether it is configured. Otherwise a stored credential owns the provider: matching OAuth invokes OAuth resolution, matching API key invokes its handler after stored env/request env merge, and a type with no matching handler returns undefined. Only an absent stored credential reaches ambient API-key auth (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts:50-117).

OAuth first checks expires with Date.now()+max(300000, minOAuthValidityMs??0) >= expires. If false, it derives request auth without calling modify. If true, it calls CredentialStore.modify and rechecks the latest stored type and expiry under the lock; a non-OAuth current value or a now-valid token returns undefined from the mutation callback, leaving that latest credential unchanged. A still-expiring OAuth credential is passed to oauth.refresh with AbortSignal.any([callerSignal, AbortSignal.timeout(15000)]). The returned rotated credential is persisted by the store before the lock is released; the post-write value, not the original optimistic snapshot, determines the result. A non-OAuth post-write value returns undefined without ambient fallback (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts:119-165).

The default five-minute window triggers refresh but does not reject a shorter-lived refreshed token. When minOAuthValidityMs was explicitly provided, the post-refresh token must satisfy the same max(five minutes, caller value) window or throw 'OAuth refresh returned a token that expires too soon for <provider>'. Thus explicitly passing zero still enforces five minutes after refresh, unlike omitting the option. The 15-second timeout is a signal passed to the provider; the refresh await itself is not separately raced against that signal, so a non-cooperative custom refresh can keep internal work/ownership pending until it settles. Caller abort still ends the public wait through the outer race, and the store's cancellation checks prevent late commit (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts:50-60; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts:135-170; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/credential-store.ts:14-55).

Finally oauth.toAuth(credential) produces {auth, source:'OAuth'} with no synthesized env field. Store read/modify failures become ModelsError code auth; refresh and toAuth failures become code oauth; API-key resolve failures become code auth. The wrapper retains the original cause and appends its formatted detail only if nonempty and not already present in the message. Exact prefixes are 'Credential store read failed for <id>', 'Credential store modify failed for <id>', 'OAuth refresh failed for <id>', 'OAuth auth derivation failed for <id>' and 'API key auth failed for provider <id>'. Existing ModelsError from modify is propagated unchanged. Failure never silently substitutes ambient auth (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts:16-42; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts:143-204).

The source tests assert stored/ambient precedence, no-handler blocking, default and longer refresh windows, no double refresh under concurrent callers, no modify for valid tokens, preservation after failure/cancellation, caller-signal propagation and wrapped cause text. They were not executed (ice:packages/ai/test/models-runtime.test.ts:617-1074).

The minimum-validity option has no finite-number validation here. Negative finite values clamp to the five-minute floor; NaN propagates through Math.max and makes the expiry comparison false, while positive Infinity makes a finite expiry always qualify and an explicit post-refresh check fail. A stricter native input validator would be a deliberate change (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/resolve.ts:135-170).

`defaultProviderAuthContext()` creates the default environment/filesystem adapter. `env(name)` reads `globalThis.process?.env` and returns the original string only if its trimmed length is nonzero; whitespace is checked without trimming the returned value. Missing process/env or a nonstring value yields undefined. `fileExists(path)` imports `node:fs/promises` through a variable module specifier, expands any leading `~` as `homedir() + path.slice(1)`, and returns true after `fs.access` succeeds. Import, home-resolution and access failures all return false; this is an accessibility probe, not a regular-file type check. No credential file is read by this adapter (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/context.ts:11-45).
entries.interfaces: AuthResolutionOverrides {apiKey?:string, env?:ProviderEnv, minOAuthValidityMs?:number, signal?:AbortSignal}; result Promise<AuthResult|undefined>, where AuthResult {auth:ModelAuth, env?:ProviderEnv, source?:string}. OAuthAuth.refresh(credential, signal)→OAuthCredential; toAuth(credential)→ModelAuth. ModelsError codes are model_source|model_validation|provider|stream|auth|oauth; only auth/oauth are produced here.
entries.dependency_text: Generic Models/ImagesModels routing to this helper belongs to AI; provider-specific refresh endpoints belong to the OAuth flow entries. Concrete provider implementations use fetch or their provider transport; no network was invoked in the audit.
entries.rust: Rust credentials::resolve has genuine provider isolation and configured/env precedence, but it falls through an empty/unresolved stored key or expired OAuth token to models.json/environment instead of retaining stored-credential authority. It does not run refresh. Native provider construction reads auth once, resolves per-provider maps and places request auth in a private ExecutionBinding; each ConfiguredProvider stream prepares from that immutable binding, injecting its stored key/headers unless request options override, with no token-expiry recheck or refresh callback. Native CLI auth refresh invokes an extension action explicitly, then separately upserts the token without a refresh lock. Preserve the private binding's rejection of caller-substituted endpoint/model headers while adding request-time credential resolution (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/credentials.rs:57-126; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider.rs:301-328; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider.rs:714-746; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider.rs:920-1029; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider/binding.rs:36-82; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider/factories.rs:237-255; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/auth.rs:159-214).
entries.port: Add a provider-scoped async auth resolver before each request binding is prepared, using the credential transaction from AUTH-002 and the explicit schema adapter from AUTH-001. Re-read/recheck inside ownership, persist rotated credentials once, and derive auth from the post-write value. Keep request override and per-field env rules explicit, retain cause/code distinctions, and preserve native endpoint/credential isolation. Implement a cooperative 15-second refresh signal and caller cancellation; if imposing a stronger hard deadline, document that as a deliberate improvement and retain ownership until abandoned work cannot commit. Do not treat manually invokable OAuth refresh as automatic request-time parity.
entries.priority_reason: Long-running sessions and concurrent requests require correct token rotation, account precedence and cancellation without credential substitution.

entries.title: Runtime credential overrides and serialized commit/synchronization
entries.what: Let a process temporarily override a provider key while preserving durable login/logout ordering and reporting when a committed credential cannot be reflected in the live model snapshot.
entries.mechanism:
A runtime key overlay can change request authentication without replacing the stored credential. A separate per-provider queue orders credential changes and live model synchronization, including failures after a successful commit.

RuntimeCredentials wraps a CredentialStore with Map<providerId, string>. set/remove change only this overlay. read checks caller cancellation then uses a truthy override, otherwise delegates; consequently an empty-string override is present for hasRuntimeApiKey/list/status but does not replace the stored credential on read. list first awaits the backing metadata list, checks cancellation, then overwrites/appends each override provider as api_key in Map order. modify always delegates to the backing store; delete checks cancellation, awaits backing deletion, then removes the overlay, so a failed delete retains the override (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/runtime-credentials.ts:4-51).

ModelRuntime adds a per-provider operation tail across login, logout, setRuntimeApiKey and removeRuntimeApiKey. Different providers may progress independently. Each queued operation waits for prior rejection to be swallowed, checks its signal, marks itself started, then runs the task. The caller races cancellation only while awaiting the started latch; once admitted it follows the operation promise. The tail is retained until settlement and deleted only if still current. API-key overlay mutation happens before change notification and synchronization. login delegates to Models.login to commit; logout delegates to Models.logout before synchronizing (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:514-532; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:556-581; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:695-710).

Synchronization checks cancellation, recomposes only the provider, rejects recorded composition error, refreshes its catalog with allowNetwork:false, propagates provider refresh error, updates the model snapshot, then refreshes that provider's availability. Every error is wrapped as CredentialSynchronizationError with providerId, operation, committed credential/undefined and cause, with message `Credential <operation> committed for <providerId>, but local synchronization failed`. No rollback of the committed state is attempted. This distinction survives cancellation after commit (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:89-109; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:534-553).
entries.interfaces: setRuntimeApiKey(providerId, key,{signal?}); removeRuntimeApiKey; login(providerId, type, AuthInteraction)→Credential; logout; listCredentials→metadata. CredentialSynchronizationOperation is exactly login|logout|setRuntimeApiKey|removeRuntimeApiKey. Runtime override status precedes stored status, configured-key status, then ambient AuthCheck.
entries.dependency_text: AUTH-002 owns backend mutation exclusion; AUTH-004 owns request-time credential resolution. The runtime operation queue is a separate layer that also serializes post-commit availability work.
entries.rust: Rust supports a selected invocation's explicit API key and durable auth CLI login/logout/refresh. Its CLI key is filtered for empty string, scoped to selected execution binding and not globally copied into unrelated providers. Provider bindings retain private request auth; this is valuable existing isolation. The inspected native auth commands commit through config upsert/remove, but do not expose a RuntimeCredentials overlay or per-provider commit-plus-live-synchronization queue/error envelope. The separate ModelRegistry only accepts explicit auth status writes and its refresh_catalog updates model metadata, not credential transactions (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider.rs:301-420; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider/binding.rs:22-96; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/auth.rs:42-72; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/auth.rs:222-240; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/model_registry.rs:214-302).
entries.port: Introduce a process-owned credential overlay with explicit semantics for empty overrides, and serialize each provider's mutation through snapshot synchronization. Return a structured committed-but-unsynchronized error so UIs do not suggest retrying a completed login blindly. Connect resulting state to the actual CLI/provider lifecycle while retaining provider identity isolation. Validate queued cancellation before admission, cancellation after commit, failed backing delete retaining override, and same-provider operation order during implementation.
entries.priority_reason: Concurrent login/logout/temporary-key operations can leave durable credentials and live model availability inconsistent without a clear recovery signal.

entries.title: Live model availability generations, snapshots and change notification
entries.what: Keep synchronous model selectors coherent while asynchronous auth and catalog checks complete out of order, and notify local observers without exposing credentials.
entries.mechanism:
The runtime exposes a synchronous model-availability snapshot while asynchronous catalog and authentication checks run. Generation counters prevent older work from publishing stale results or clearing newer errors.

Snapshot fields are all, available, configuredProviders, storedProviders and auth. A rebuild clears collection/composition errors, recomposes IDs in insertion order, then sets all and provisionally filters by the previous configuredProviders set. A native extension base precedes a builtin. No overlays means use that base object unchanged; overlay composition failure records an error and restores the base if one exists, otherwise deletes the provider (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:255-303).

A full availability pass runs getAvailable, all checkAuth calls and credential metadata list concurrently. Only the latest availabilityRefreshSeq may publish; only its captured availabilityErrorSeq may clear the shared error. Queuing a full pass increments every provider-specific generation too. A targeted credential refresh increments the full generation, then its provider generation and error generation; it concurrently fetches that provider's available models/AuthCheck/credential, checks cancellation, and publishes only if its provider generation still matches. It preserves unrelated provider state and rebuilds available in current all-model order using `(provider + NUL + id)` keys. An old or aborted failure cannot overwrite the current error. Direct getAvailable(providerId) returns fresh results and manages the latest error but does not publish the global availability snapshot (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:305-406; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:424-459).

subscribeChanges stores callbacks in a Set. notifyChange coalesces calls into one microtask, resets pending before snapshot-dispatching listeners, ignores listener throws and returns an unsubscribe closure. Notifications have no credentials or provider response payload. getError joins config error, provider-labeled composition errors and availability error with blank lines. refresh always reloads models.json and Radius bases; targeted options recompose unique selected IDs, otherwise all. Catalog refresh defaults allowNetwork to the constructor's ICE_OFFLINE policy. Older Models.refresh returning undefined gets an empty error map fallback. Snapshot updates precede availability refresh; targeted availability failures enter result.errors unless caller aborted, whereas full-pass failure remains getError-only. Final result combines catalog/caller abort status and collected errors (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:154-173; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:450-459; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:712-754).

Native registration rejects whitespace-only IDs, removes legacy extension config, recomposes, snapshots and starts an unawaited offline refresh. Legacy registration eagerly validates the incoming config before mutation, merges only defined fields over the old config, removes native registration, then recomposes. Stored/configured auth creates provisional availability without replacing a real auth check. Unregister removes both extension layers and reveals any underlying builtin/config provider before offline refresh (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:756-809).

Adjacent public guidance formatters return `/login` help with resolved providers.md and models.md paths. No-model-available prepends `No models available. `; no-model-selected uses two blank-line-separated help/selection sections and `Then use /model to select a model.`. No-API-key displays `the selected model` only when provider equals literal `unknown`, otherwise the supplied provider, followed by login help (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/auth-guidance.ts:4-24). These formatters do not probe or mutate credentials.
entries.interfaces: subscribeChanges(listener)→unsubscribe; getAvailableSnapshot synchronous; getAvailable async; refresh({providers?, allowNetwork?, force?, signal?})→{aborted, errors:Map}; getError aggregates diagnostics. Snapshot authentication is a configured check, not a guaranteed successful remote login.

It has no corresponding generation guards or coalesced observer contract. Source search across crates found ModelRegistry::new and refresh_catalog only in its definition/tests; production CLI resolution instead builds catalog and private runtimes in provider.rs. entries.title: Credential-blind models.json validation and ultra compatibility
entries.what: Load one immutable model configuration without resolving credentials, and accept every supported reasoning level and per-model setting without invalidating otherwise usable providers.
entries.mechanism:
Model configuration is parsed and validated as one immutable snapshot before any credential expression is resolved. The snapshot retains provider order and supports the complete TypeScript reasoning vocabulary, including ultra.

ModelConfig.load(undefined) and ENOENT return an empty successful Map. A supplied path is normalized and read as UTF-8. Other I/O errors, comment-JSON parse errors and schema errors become distinct getError strings with the normalized `File: <path>`; callers receive an empty Map rather than a thrown exception. Validation runs before any provider is accepted. Required-field diagnostics append the first required property to dot-separated instancePath; all validation errors are emitted as `  - <path>: <message>`. Successful providers retain Object.entries order and are recursively Object.freeze'd; getProvider returns the frozen value, getProviderIds a fresh ordered array (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-config.ts:206-287).

Root requires providers:Record<string, ProviderConfig>. Provider fields are name/baseUrl/apiKey/api (nonempty strings when present), oauth exactly "radius", string headers, compat, authHeader:boolean, models array and modelOverrides map. Model definitions require nonempty id; name/api/baseUrl are optional nonempty strings; reasoning, thinkingLevelMap, input text/image array, complete four-rate cost plus optional tiers, contextWindow/maxTokens numbers, serviceTiers:string[], samplingParams:Record<string, unknown>, string headers and compat are optional. Overrides omit id/api/baseUrl, allow partial four-rate cost and mergeable thinking/sampling/compat data. TypeBox numeric schema itself does not impose positivity; model construction separately rejects explicitly nonpositive contextWindow/maxTokens. No credential expression executes during this load (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-config.ts:129-204; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:131-168).

thinkingLevelMap explicitly accepts off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra, each optional string or null. The TS public reasoning union also includes ultra. Compat schema covers Completions/Responses/Anthropic unions, nested OpenRouter/Vercel routing, chat-template variables `$var:thinking.enabled|thinking.effort` with omitWhenOff, token field choice, session affinity, strict tools and protocol-specific switches. Extra-property rejection is not requested in these Type.Object declarations; do not treat this as a strict unknown-field rejection contract (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-config.ts:10-127; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:80-91).

The shared parseJsonWithComments helper first calls strict JSON.parse. Only after that throws, stripJsonComments applies two regex passes: each recognizes and preserves complete double-quoted string literals; the first removes // line comments through the next LF, and the second removes a comma followed by whitespace and a closing brace/bracket while retaining that whitespace and closer. Block comments are not stripped. The second JSON.parse failure propagates to ModelConfig's parse-diagnostic boundary. The direct suite verifies comment-like URL/string contents, line comments with trailing commas, and rejection of malformed unquoted keys (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/json.ts:1-16; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/json-utils.test.ts:1-18).
entries.interfaces: ModelConfig.load(modelsJsonPath?)→Promise<ModelConfig>; getProvider/getProviderIds/getError. This is an immutable config snapshot, not a secret resolver or a writer. Diagnostics distinguish load, parse and invalid-schema failures.
entries.dependency_text: AUTH-008 applies semantic model defaults/overlay rules. AI-005 owns shared thinking levels, Ultra, and clamp behavior. Configuration-expression execution belongs SET-005/006 and is deferred until auth/request resolution. AUTH-033 enumerates every compatibility configuration field and nested schema.
entries.rust:
Rust loads a typed ModelsConfig whose providers are IndexMap-ordered. Missing file yields empty config; invalid data returns ConfigError. Parsing tries standard JSON then a custom // comment stripper, retaining the original error if both fail. Its ProviderConfig/ModelDefinition omit TS modelOverrides, provider compat/oauth and several model options, and per-model api is not represented. Critically ThinkingLevelMap is BTreeMap<ThinkingLevel, Option<String>> while ThinkingLevel has Off through Max only; a JSON `ultra` map key therefore fails serde decoding of the entire configuration, rather than merely being ignored. Native save serializes the fixed typed shape, with backup then atomic write, so unknown fields are not retained by a rewrite (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:343-493; rust:crates/ice-ai/src/types.rs:489-507).

Active ICE_PORTING.md §11a 670–675 describes the same ultra incompatibility. Its claim about three keys remapped during a prior import cannot be verified here because actual user auth/models state is outside the permitted read scope. The source-level schema gap is independently established; no import was performed by this audit.

The concrete native parser is parse_models_json and its string-aware strip_line_comments/find_line_comment helpers. It preserves // inside double-quoted strings and handles escapes, but does not strip trailing commas or block comments. It returns the first strict serde error if the stripped parse also fails, whereas TS propagates its second JSON.parse error (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:505-554).
entries.port: Add ultra to the shared reasoning representation and every parser/serializer/order boundary before importing TS model maps. Implement the credential-blind TS configuration schema and separate load/parse/schema diagnostics while retaining native ordered provider storage and durable write behavior. Add explicit treatment for unknown fields and import format rather than silently discarding future settings. Cover one malformed provider causing whole-snapshot failure, ultra keys, null unsupported levels, required-path diagnostics and nonpositive semantic limits in implementation tests.
entries.priority_reason: A valid TS ultra map currently prevents native models.json from loading at all, and omitted override fields change provider behavior.

entries.title: Provider composition order, model overrides and extension registration
entries.what: Combine built-in catalogs, models.json and extension providers deterministically while keeping configured context windows and per-model overrides authoritative.
entries.mechanism:
Provider composition combines built-in models, user configuration and extensions in a defined order. Later overrides can replace specific fields or whole catalogs, while request secrets remain separate from public model descriptors.

The base is nativeExtensionProviders.get(id) before builtin. Models.json starts with base models copied in order, changing baseUrl unless oauth is radius and shallow/deep-subfield merging compat. Empty/no-op config is rejected unless it supplies models/baseUrl/headers/compat/nonempty modelOverrides/apiKey/oauth or defined authHeader; oauth requires baseUrl. The models array upserts by exact case-sensitive id using the first existing duplicate's index; defaults for api/baseUrl come from the same-id model or first model. New definition defaults are name=id, reasoning=false, input=[text], all costs 0, contextWindow 128000, maxTokens16384; explicit limits<=0 throw. Model definitions do not otherwise inherit metadata from an existing model and public constructed models have headers undefined (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:131-213).

Legacy extension config with no models changes only baseUrl when supplied; with models present, even [], it replaces the catalog, resolves each api/baseUrl from definition→extension→same-id/first base model, spreads definition metadata and clears public headers. Missing api/baseUrl throws. Then extension OAuth modifyModels may transform the list using the last published OAuth credential. Explicit contextWindow in models.json definitions is re-applied after extension replacement/refresh; finally modelOverrides applies name/reasoning/input/context/output/service tiers, fieldwise costs (tiers replace), merged thinkingLevelMap/samplingParams and compat. Compat merges top-level keys, plus one shallow merge for openRouterRouting, vercelGatewayRouting, chatTemplateKwargs, chatTemplateArgs; arrays/nested grandchildren are not recursively merged. Model override headers are resolved separately for requests (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:81-129; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:215-246; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:437-467).

Provider name precedence is extension.name→config.name→base.name→extension.oauth.name→id; provider baseUrl is extension→config→base. Auth requires at least API key or OAuth method. stream/streamSimple use lazyStream: extension.streamSimple wins when model.api matches extension.api for both entry points; else base dispatch is used only if some current base model advertises that API; else getApiProvider(model.api), error if absent. fetchDeferred/cancelDeferred are forwarded only from base. refresh runs base hook first, then extension.refreshModels if present; after signal check one publish update validates refreshed extension models before installing them and updates the OAuth credential. filterModels is forwarded from base (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:417-541).

Registration first validates incoming config independently (streamSimple requires extension.api) before touching old state. Re-registration merges only defined fields; undefined preserves prior values. Radius aliases from models.json oauth:"radius" replace the built-in map entry and strip one trailing /v1 or /v1/ before constructing the gateway. Native/legacy extension registration are mutually exclusive for the ID; unregister reveals builtin/config layers (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:238-253; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:756-809).
entries.interfaces: ProviderConfigInput supports optional name/baseUrl/apiKey/api/streamSimple/headers/authHeader/OAuth/models/refreshModels. ExtensionOAuthConfig uses legacy callbacks plus refreshToken/getApiKey/modifyModels. UsesCallbackServer is deprecated and ignored by canonical flows. Models are returned synchronously from composed getModels after eager structural validation.
entries.dependency_text: AUTH-007 owns immutable config validation; AUTH-009 owns secret/header evaluation. AI-003 owns registered wire API dispatch; extension registration transport is the EXT area.
entries.rust: Native provider resolution already merges built-in Anthropic/OpenAI catalogs, extension manifest models and user config, selects extension factory by provider ID plus API, and groups multiple wire bindings under one public provider. User model merge replaces a matching provider/API plus case-insensitive model id or appends. Native provider_to_models supports only Anthropic/Completions/Responses from provider-level api, defaults omitted api to Anthropic and omitted endpoint to protocol default, sets context_window 0 when unspecified, and merges model headers before provider headers (provider wins). It does not implement TS per-model API selection, modelOverrides, extension replacement/modifyModels, context-window final override order or the TS semantic defaults. Model headers are subsequently stripped from public descriptors and kept in private ExecutionBinding; preserve that native protection (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider.rs:714-920; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider/factories.rs:110-275; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:808-934; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider/binding.rs:22-96). The exact native max_tokens initializer at config.rs887 was redacted in this read and is not used as evidence of a default.
entries.port: Build a single ordered composition service with explicit base→models.json→extension→configured-context-window→modelOverrides phases. Keep public descriptor/private execution separation while evaluating headers at request time. Match exact-ID upserts, extension [] replacement, partial registration merge and validation rollback. Extend protocol selection per model instead of interpreting provider identity as a protocol alias. Ensure caller tests cover conflicting defaults, multiple APIs for one provider, refreshed extension models and null thinking overrides.
entries.priority_reason: Incorrect merge order silently changes endpoints, context limits, available models and extension behavior across nearly every custom provider.

entries.source:
ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:248-415; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:544-591; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:111-125; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:490-511; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:595-693. ice:packages/coding-agent/test/model-registry.test.ts:1440-2052; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/model-runtime-auth-options.test.ts:1-293.

Exported symbols: `ResolvedRequestAuth` (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-registry.ts:17).
Exported symbols: `ModelRuntimeAuthOverrides` (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:82).
Exported symbols: `AuthStatus`, `clearApiKeyCache`, `resolveConfiguredModelHeaders`, `CompatibilityRequestConfig`, `resolveCompatibilityRequestConfig`, `configuredRequestAuthStatus` (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:73; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:79; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:544; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:557; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:562; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:577).
entries.what: Resolve secrets only when needed, merge configured/request headers in the correct order and retain provider-specific endpoint and environment overrides through all request types.
entries.mechanism:
Request preparation resolves provider authentication and combines configured, model and caller headers in separate stages. It then passes the resulting credentials, environment and endpoint to streaming or deferred operations.

Configured key precedence is extension.apiKey??modelsJson.apiKey; provider raw headers merge config then extension. API-key auth inherits base login/name/check/resolve when available. An OAuth-only base with no inherited API-key auth and no configured key gets no fabricated API-key login. A stored credential is authoritative and resolves through inherited auth (or its own truthy key); configured keys are considered only without a stored credential. check treats command expressions as configured without executing them and validates referenced env names; resolve executes the configured expression using AuthContext env. Header env starts with credential.env then result.env and fills only absent referenced names from AuthContext. Header expansion uses strict SET-005/006 logic. authHeader defaults false; if true it requires a truthy resolved apiKey and finally writes Authorization:`Bearer <key>`, otherwise throws `authHeader requires a resolved API key` (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:268-375).

Legacy OAuth adapts onAuth/onDeviceCode/onPrompt/onProgress/onManualCodeInput/onSelect to typed notify/prompt, forwards signal, forces type:oauth after login/refresh, and turns getApiKey into ModelAuth. OAuth toAuth merges configured headers using credential.env if it is an object, then applies authHeader. Per-model raw header precedence is modelOverrides[id].headers→modelsJson.models exact-id definition.headers→extension.models exact-id headers. Public model header objects are not populated by composition. Runtime getAuth(model) obtains generic Models auth, resolves model headers against result.env overlaid by explicit env, then merges case-insensitively: remove all old spellings of each overriding name, retain the new spelling/value including null deletion markers (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:248-266; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:377-415; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:544-555; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:111-125; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:490-511).

prepareRequest looks up provider first (ModelsError category provider if unknown), resolves auth with apiKey/env/signal overrides (auth error if unconfigured), case-insensitively merges request headers over auth headers, then awaits optional transformHeaders on the resulting object. It strips transformHeaders from provider options, merges result.env then request.env, applies credential baseUrl to a cloned input model when truthy, and uses request.apiKey??resolved.apiKey. stream and streamSimple are lazy; complete variants await stream.result. fetchDeferred runs the same preparation in lazyStream and rejects unsupported capability; cancelDeferred prepares directly then awaits provider.cancelDeferred, rejecting missing capability (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:595-693).

Compatibility ModelRegistry fallback resolves configured provider/model headers even without auth, but returns a specific no-key error when authHeader is required. It unwraps Error.cause message and maps the authHeader sentinel to `No API key found for "<provider>"`. This best-effort compatibility API does not make canonical streaming accept an unconfigured provider (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-registry.ts:69-98).

`clearApiKeyCache` is a public declaration at ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:79 and a re-export at ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-registry.ts:26. The connector redacts its initializer, so its exact assignment remains unverified. The visible import names `clearConfigValueCache`, whose separate implementation clears `commandResultCache`; that observation does not establish the hidden alias bytes (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:25-33; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:79; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-registry.ts:26; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/resolve-config-value.ts:285-288).
entries.interfaces:
getAuth(providerId|model,{apiKey?, env?, signal?, minOAuthValidityMs?}); transformHeaders may return ProviderHeaders asynchronously. Header values support null through ProviderHeaders. stream/complete, streamSimple/completeSimple, fetchDeferred/cancelDeferred all share request preparation.

`ResolvedRequestAuth` is `{ok:true,apiKey?:string,headers?:ProviderHeaders,baseUrl?:string,env?:Record<string,string>} | {ok:false,error:string}`. `ModelRuntimeAuthOverrides` extends the optional signal input with optional apiKey/env/minOAuthValidityMs. `CompatibilityRequestConfig` has optional headers and required authHeader:boolean. `AuthStatus` has configured:boolean, optional label and optional source exactly stored|runtime|environment|fallback|models_json_key|models_json_command. These DTOs add no independent runtime validation; `configuredRequestAuthStatus` reports a command expression as configured without execution, resolves referenced environment availability, otherwise labels extension key as fallback and configured key as models_json_key (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-registry.ts:17-25; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:82-87; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:73-77; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:557-591).
entries.dependency_text: AUTH-004 defines credential selection/refresh. AUTH-008 keeps composition credential-blind. SET-005/006 own config expression grammar/cache/deadline. AI-002/003 own generic Models/stream adapters.
entries.rust: Native ExecutionBinding owns canonical model endpoint/headers and auth, checks provider+API+case-insensitive model id and restores the bound model, ignoring caller descriptor changes. Request options may override the key and merge headers case-insensitively; bound key/header injection only happens when options.api_key is None. Native headers are string maps and do not express TS null deletion markers. Config header expressions are resolved during catalog construction, with model then provider precedence, using lenient omission of unresolved values. No equivalent transformHeaders, credential environment per request, credential baseUrl derivation or shared deferred fetch/cancel path appears in the inspected binding/factories. Preserve native endpoint isolation while adding the missing preparation behavior rather than copying mutable public model execution authority (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider/binding.rs:22-104; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider/factories.rs:50-109; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:606-620; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:893-934).
entries.port: Separate public model selection from private request materialization; add a canonical auth/header preparation stage after authoritative endpoint selection. Support null header removal, strict configured-header errors, model-over-provider/request precedence and asynchronous transforms with cancellation. Refresh secrets on each request without leaking them into catalog snapshots. Extend deferred operations through the same auth path when protocol support is added.
entries.priority_reason: Header/credential precedence errors can send an unusable request or route one provider's credential to unintended execution configuration.

Exported symbols: `ModelsStoreOperationOptions`, `InMemoryModelsStore` (ice:packages/ai/src/models-store.ts:16; ice:packages/ai/src/models-store.ts:27).
Exported symbols: `CreateModelRuntimeOptions` (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:66).

entries.what: Restore dynamic models without blocking startup on write locks, refresh them conditionally, and retain a usable baseline catalog when the upstream service is unavailable.
entries.mechanism:
Remote model catalogs are restored from persistent overlays before optional network refresh. Validators, freshness timestamps and bundled catalog dates determine whether a stored or fetched overlay becomes visible.

ModelsStoreEntry is models plus optional lastModified/checkedAt/etag; etag retains server quotes. Both in-memory stores structuredClone on read/write and check caller cancellation before mutation. FileModelsStore defaults to agentDir/models-store.json and reuses FileAuthStorageBackend for locked whole-document RMW. Reads are lock-free atomic-replacement snapshots; concurrent reads share only the current in-flight Promise, cleared on success or failure. A caller races its own signal without cancelling that shared snapshot read. File writes/deletes parse the current root, change only one provider and serialize two-space JSON under the backend lock (ice:packages/ai/src/models-store.ts:1-46; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/models-store.ts:9-74).

withRemoteCatalog overlays a static provider using exact case-sensitive model id: replace in baseline position, append unknown IDs. On every refresh it first publishes a stored overlay filtered to the provider ID. Stored models are ignored when a bundled generation timestamp exists and stored lastModified is missing or <=that timestamp. Without a bundled timestamp, any stored model body is eligible. A false publish result stops the hook. Network work requires allowNetwork and a non-aborted signal. Unless force, checkedAt and lastModified must both be present and Date.now()-checkedAt<4h to skip fetching; a future checkedAt also meets that comparison (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/remote-catalog-provider.ts:7-79).

Fetch GET new URL(`/api/models/providers/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`, base), default base https://pi.dev, with accept:application/json, Ice User-Agent and if-none-match only when stored.models is nonempty and etag truthy. 304 with stored data persists only refreshed checkedAt. 404/501 persist the previous body (or []) with checkedAt, lastModified0, etag undefined and clear the live dynamic overlay. Other non-OK responses persist prior body/validator plus checkedAt then throw `Model catalog request failed for <id>: <status>`; if prior lastModified existed this also starts the ordinary four-hour throttle unless forced. Success accepts an array, object.models array, or Object.values of an object, filters only object/non-null/has-id and forces provider=id; it does not validate a complete Model shape. Invalid top-level primitive throws. last-modified is Date.parse or 0, etag retained, and publish persists the complete entry even if the bundled timestamp suppresses its live overlay. Signal is checked after fetch and after body decode (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/remote-catalog-provider.ts:19-133).

ModelRuntime.create uses default auth storage unless injected; modelsPath:null disables config and chooses in-memory catalog storage unless a store is injected. Otherwise models-store.json defaults beside models.json. Every builtin except Radius gets the remote wrapper with generated catalog timestamp. ICE_OFFLINE being present disables default network refresh regardless of its value; create allows network only with allowModelNetwork===true and that policy. Optional create timeout is linked with caller signal; initial refresh is awaited and timer cleared (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:193-235).
entries.interfaces:
ModelsStore read/write/delete with signal; Provider.refreshModels receives stored/allowNetwork/force/signal/publish. File read does not wait on a held/leaked write lock. Remote freshness is 4*60*60*1000 ms and depends on both checkedAt and lastModified.

`ModelsStoreOperationOptions` is `{signal?:AbortSignal}`. `CreateModelRuntimeOptions` carries optional credentials, authPath, modelsPath:string|null, modelsStore, modelsStorePath, allowModelNetwork, modelRefreshTimeoutMs, catalogBaseUrl and signal. It names the injected store/path/network/timeout inputs for the create-time restoration described above; modelsPath:null has the in-memory/config-disable semantics specified in this entry (ice:packages/ai/src/models-store.ts:16-18; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:66-80).

entries.what: Make the same provider identities discoverable with their own endpoint, authentication environment and wire API choices instead of assuming protocol compatibility supplies a catalog.
entries.mechanism:
Built-in provider declarations connect stable provider identities to names, endpoints, authentication and wire APIs. Catalog assembly preserves declaration order and keeps image-provider discovery separate from text-provider discovery.

builtinProviders returns 39 fresh provider objects in declaration order: amazon-bedrock, ant-ling, anthropic, azure-openai-responses, baseten, cerebras, cloudflare-ai-gateway, cloudflare-workers-ai, deepseek, fireworks, github-copilot, google, google-vertex, groq, huggingface, kimi-coding, minimax, minimax-cn, mistral, moonshotai, moonshotai-cn, nvidia, openai, openai-codex, opencode, opencode-go, openrouter, qwen-token-plan, qwen-token-plan-cn, radius, together, vercel-ai-gateway, xai, xiaomi, xiaomi-token-plan-ams, xiaomi-token-plan-cn, xiaomi-token-plan-sgp, zai, zai-coding-cn. builtinModels creates a collection and sets each in that order. Each generated *.models.ts wrapper imports data/<id>.json and flattens protocol groups with Object.assign({},...Object.values(groups)); later duplicate model IDs replace earlier values. The provider argument is a type-level selector and is unused by that runtime flattening. getBuiltinModels returns values or[]; provider keys come from MODELS; generated timestamp uses Date.parse and yields undefined on NaN. Radius is dynamically constructed and not a generated MODELS key (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/all.ts:45-153; ice:packages/ai/src/model-catalog.ts:1-28).

The remaining identities have explicit specialized auth contracts: amazon-bedrock and google-vertex in AUTH-012; both Cloudflare providers in AUTH-013; Radius in AUTH-014. Anthropic uses https://api.anthropic.com and anthropic-messages with API-key plus lazy subscription OAuth; its key handler prefers stored key, then authorization-token headers, OAuth-token/key fallback, with the exact auth resolution reviewed separately. GitHub Copilot uses https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com and supports anthropic-messages, openai-completions, openai-responses; API key env is COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN plus OAuth. Its filterModels narrows only when an OAuth credential contains an all-string availableModelIds array; empty valid array means no models, malformed/missing list leaves the catalog unchanged (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/anthropic.ts:9-55; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/github-copilot.ts:9-34).

Image-generation providers are a separate fresh list containing only openrouterImagesProvider. It shares ID/name/API-key and lazy OAuth with text OpenRouter but uses IMAGE_MODELS.openrouter and wire openrouter-images. The image API lazy registration caches its import Promise, catches import/generation errors into an AssistantImages error result with empty output, model identifiers and Date.now timestamp, and registers at module import (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/openrouter-images.ts:8-22; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/images/register-builtins.ts:1-50).

This entry verifies declaration/assembly code, not every generated JSON model payload. Those catalog payloads and general API implementations require their own AI source evidence. The displayed provider endpoints are defaults, not remote service availability claims.

Each individually named `*_MODELS` export in field 2 is the generated TypeScript wrapper around `flattenModelCatalog(providerId, values)`. Its declaration was read and matched to the assembly mechanism; this adds no claim that all underlying generated JSON rows were source-reviewed. The generation notice/imports were additionally checked in amazon-bedrock.models.ts:1-8. `getBuiltinModel` directly indexes the catalog and may return undefined at runtime despite its non-optional TypeScript return assertion; `getBuiltinProviders` returns its enumerable keys, while timestamp parsing returns undefined for NaN (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/all.ts:52-75).
entries.interfaces:
Provider IDs are credential/config identities. API protocols may be shared; e.g. opencode/opencode-go share OPENCODE_API_KEY and Moonshot regions share MOONSHOT_API_KEY deliberately. OpenAI Codex has no fabricated API-key login. Display name, login labels and endpoint can differ from the provider ID.

`ModelGroups = Record<string, Record<string, object>>`; `BuiltinProvider = keyof typeof MODELS`. These compile-time aliases identify the flattening input and generated-provider key set, rather than adding validation of catalog payloads (ice:packages/ai/src/model-catalog.ts:3; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/all.ts:52).
entries.dependency_text: AUTH-004 defines generic auth resolution; specialized auth/catalog behavior has separate entries. AI-002/003 own generated model content/general API lifecycle and wire dispatch. Image generation API implementation is AI-area work.
entries.rust:
Core Rust compiles Anthropic and OpenAI Responses catalogs and allows user models plus loaded extension manifests. Native wire factories cover Anthropic Messages, OpenAI Completions and OpenAI Responses; a protocol implementation alone does not supply the other TS provider identities/defaults. Native environment fallback is intentionally limited to Anthropic/OpenAI; package manifests may declare apiKeyEnv/requiresAuth, and arbitrary custom IDs require explicit configuration. Preserve this identity isolation rather than synthesizing env names from IDs (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider.rs:859-920; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider/factories.rs:20-109; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/credentials.rs:49-126; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:828-850).

Frozen Rust docs explicitly move concrete DeepSeek/OpenRouter/llama.cpp/Proxy implementations to an independent ice-package repository. Their implementation parity is unverified here; generic native package support is real and remains credited. The initial Rust tree has no compiled zai/opencode/opencode-go catalog declarations corresponding to this TS array. Active ICE_PORTING.md §11a 676–680 also names Modal in prior imported credentials, but Modal is not a TS builtin in this inspected array, and no actual user credential counts were read (rust:docs/architecture/provider-packages.md:3-23; rust:docs/extensions/provider-integration.md:8-19).
entries.port: Port provider declarations/catalog packaging with explicit ID/name/default URL/env/API tuples, preferably as native provider packages where the architecture intends them. Preserve separate regional identities and shared-env choices, built-in order, generated-data precedence and account-specific filters. Do not mark an external package complete until its source is reviewed in an authorized scope. Bring zai/opencode/opencode-go catalogs into a usable native discovery path without treating historical Modal credentials as proof of a missing built-in.

entries.what: Support cloud-native credentials without requiring a copied API key, and preserve provider-scoped profile/project/location settings from login through request execution.
entries.mechanism:
Bedrock and Vertex can authenticate through cloud credential chains without a copied API key. Their login and readiness checks preserve provider-scoped environment fields for the downstream cloud transport.

Bedrock login first checks cancellation and offers bearer-token, aws-profile, credential-chain. Bearer returns api_key with secret prompt value. Other choices emit AWS credential-chain guidance; aws-profile returns api_key with env.AWS_PROFILE, credential-chain waits for a confirmation text prompt and returns api_key with no key. Unknown selection throws. Its resolver wraps each ambient env read with cancellation checks and uses this exact branch order: truthy stored key→apiKey plus credential.env; ambient AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK→auth{}; stored env.AWS_PROFILE ?? ambient AWS_PROFILE when truthy→auth{} plus stored env; paired AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY→auth{}; ECS relative URI, ECS full URI, web identity file→auth{}; otherwise undefined. Stored empty AWS_PROFILE masks ambient at this nullish branch. The resolver reports the source label, but leaves ambient AWS token/chain use to the wire API rather than copying token bytes into ModelAuth. Session credential env is supplied by the generic resolver (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/amazon-bedrock.ts:11-89).

Vertex login offers api-key, adc, service-account with cancellation before/after selection. API-key returns the secret prompt value. Unknown selection throws. ADC/service-account emits setup guidance, asks project and location, optionally credentials file, and returns an api_key credential carrying only env fields. Resolve picks credential.key??GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY; truthy key succeeds. Otherwise ADC path is credential.env.GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS??ambient value??`~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json`; fileExists is awaited with cancellation checks. Project uses credential.env.GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT??ambient GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT??GCLOUD_PROJECT; location uses credential.env.GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION??ambient. Only existing credentials file plus truthy project/location yields auth{} and stored env. A stored empty field masks fallback under these nullish expressions; presence of any credential determines its stored-source label (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/google-vertex.ts:6-99).

The legacy env-api-keys utility has a separate synchronous readiness probe. It lazily imports Node fs/os/path without awaiting module initialization. Vertex explicit provider-env credentials path bypasses the shared ADC cache; the ambient/default-file result is process-cached only after Node helpers are ready (in browser the negative result can cache). It returns the sentinel `<authenticated>` only with ADC plus project/location. Bedrock returns that sentinel for AWS profile, access-key pair, bearer, ECS relative/full URI or web identity file. This utility does not itself resolve or copy cloud credentials. It is not equivalent to the canonical asynchronous auth resolver (ice:packages/ai/src/env-api-keys.ts:1-67; ice:packages/ai/src/env-api-keys.ts:140-188).

The legacy `findEnvKeys` overloads share one implementation: obtain the provider's ordered environment-name list, filter on truthy `getProviderEnvValue`, and return undefined when no list or no value survives. `getEnvApiKey` uses the first found value, except Anthropic selects the first name other than `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN_ENV`; if none qualifies it continues to the Vertex/Bedrock ambient readiness probes already specified above, then returns undefined. Each pair of signature overload records refers to this one runtime implementation. The three exported Anthropic environment-name constant declarations were visible but their initializer strings were connector-redacted; the exact initializer bytes are not newly certified here (ice:packages/ai/src/env-api-keys.ts:29-31; ice:packages/ai/src/env-api-keys.ts:128-188).

entries.dependency_text: AUTH-001 preserves credential env shape; AUTH-004/009 propagate it. AI-003 owns actual cloud wire/SDK implementation, signing, region/proxy behavior and ambient credential chain execution. Merely recognizing readiness does not implement those protocols.
entries.rust: Rust Api recognizes BedrockConverseStream and GoogleVertex strings, but the core CLI factory set only supplies Anthropic, OpenAI Completions and OpenAI Responses. Native credentials::resolve supports provider-declared API-key env and anonymous manifests, plus stored fixed OAuth/key forms; it has no cloud-profile/ADC login interaction or corresponding keyless credential readiness branches. The generic extension OAuth interface can host a future cloud login but does not implement these choices or AWS/Google execution itself. Concrete external ice-package implementations remain unverified (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/types.rs:460-475; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider/factories.rs:20-109; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/credentials.rs:49-126; rust:crates/ice-extensions/src/oauth.rs:120-137).

Keep readiness checks separate from actual credentials acquisition/signing. Match nullish-versus-truthy precedence, cancellation around I/O and the legacy cache only where compatibility requires it. Add implementation checks for ADC missing/project missing, explicit empty fields, stored profiles, AWS chain sources and no accidental cross-provider credential fallback.

entries.what: Keep Cloudflare API credentials, account/gateway identifiers and upstream authentication distinct, including gateway requests that intentionally remove inherited upstream auth headers.
entries.mechanism:
Cloudflare authentication combines a token with account and optional gateway identifiers. Gateway requests carry that token separately from upstream authentication and can explicitly remove inherited auth headers.

Workers login asks secret API key then text account ID; Gateway adds text gateway ID. Both store type:api_key, key and provider env fields. Per-field resolution prefers a defined credential value (key for the API-key field, env[name] for other fields) and otherwise awaits AuthContext.env with cancellation before/after. A defined empty value masks ambient fallback, then fails the final truthiness check. All require key and account; Gateway additionally requires gateway. Resolved env contains account and gateway when truthy. Source is stored credential whenever any credential object was provided, even if some fields came from ambient env. The constant initializer at cloudflare-auth.ts4 was redacted, but the visible provider documentation identifies its intended environment name as CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/cloudflare-auth.ts:4-51; ice:packages/coding-agent/docs/providers.md:82-83; ice:packages/coding-agent/docs/providers.md:243-275).

Workers returns auth.apiKey. Gateway returns only headers: `cf-aig-authorization:Bearer <key>`, `Authorization:null`, `x-api-key:null`, preventing default upstream credentials from being synthesized unless a later configured/request header overrides the deletion marker. Login functions themselves do not add explicit abort checks between prompts; interaction and outer auth machinery carry cancellation. This differs from the cloud login functions with explicit bracketing (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/cloudflare-auth.ts:54-103).

cloudflareStreams wraps both full/simple stream entry points and materializes every `{CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID}` and `{CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY_ID}` occurrence in model.baseUrl from options.env. Missing env leaves placeholders literal; no env or unchanged URL returns the original model object, otherwise a shallow clone. It neither URL-encodes values nor changes provider/model identity. Workers uses OpenAI Completions; Gateway supports Anthropic, Completions and Responses with the same materializer (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/cloudflare-stream.ts:1-29; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/cloudflare-ai-gateway.ts:1-24; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/cloudflare-workers-ai.ts:1-16).
entries.interfaces:
Credential.env.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID required; Gateway also CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY_ID. ProviderHeaders must support null as removal. Request endpoint placeholders are substituted from scoped env, not mutated globally.

Exact source endpoint constants: `CLOUDFLARE_WORKERS_AI_BASE_URL = 'https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID}/ai/v1'`; `CLOUDFLARE_AI_GATEWAY_COMPAT_BASE_URL = 'https://gateway.ai.cloudflare.com/v1/{CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID}/{CLOUDFLARE_GATEWAY_ID}/compat'`; the OPENAI and ANTHROPIC gateway constants use the same prefix with `/openai` and `/anthropic` respectively. Placeholder replacement remains the scoped-env materialization described above (ice:packages/ai/src/api/cloudflare.ts:1-15).
entries.dependency_text: AUTH-009 must preserve null headers and configured inline upstream auth override order; AI-003 owns wire-specific default-header removal and HTTP dispatch.
entries.rust: Native headers and credential env are BTreeMap<String, String>, and ModelAuth-style header deletion markers are absent. A user can configure a concrete Cloudflare URL/header and native has_header_auth recognizes cf-aig-authorization, but this does not provide the typed login/env prerequisites, key isolation or template materialization. Core wire implementations can route compatible configured requests; generic package support is therefore credited while provider-specific behavior is missing in the audited tree (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:232-273; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:359-407; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/credentials.rs:129-141; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider/binding.rs:53-96).
entries.port: Add Cloudflare provider auth methods and scoped endpoint templates, with explicit header-removal representation carried into each wire API. Keep gateway token and upstream Authorization separate; allow later user-configured inline BYOK headers according to AUTH-009. Preserve credential-field empty masking and account/gateway requirement errors. Verify all supported wire APIs, mixed stored/ambient fields and provider/env isolation in implementation.
entries.priority_reason: Gateway requests need a distinct credential/header contract; treating the Cloudflare token as an upstream API key breaks authentication.
