entries.what: Discover models from a Radius gateway, restore them offline and migrate old OAuth-embedded catalogs without losing the current provider identity.
entries.mechanism:
A Radius provider restores stored models and can fetch a fresh gateway configuration when network access is enabled. It also migrates legacy OAuth-embedded catalogs while retaining the configured provider identity.

radiusProvider options default id radius, name Radius, gateway https://radius.pi.dev. URL normalization prepends https:// unless the value starts with http:// or https:// case-insensitively, then strips all trailing slashes. It does not otherwise parse/validate the URL. Initial models are empty. Auth offers RADIUS_API_KEY plus a lazy OAuth flow receiving name/gateway. stream and streamSimple forward to ice-messages (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/radius.ts:13-34; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/radius.ts:79-81; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/radius-config.ts:53-74; ice:packages/ai/src/utils/legacy-protocol.ts:1-3).

Gateway config is {baseUrl:string, models:array}. Sanitizer rejects nonobject/array roots or missing wrong-typed fields, then filters model rows requiring object/nonarray, id/name strings, reasoning boolean, input array, cost object/nonarray, contextWindow/maxTokens numbers. It does not validate input elements, rate fields, thinking maps, number finiteness or positivity. Accepted rows are shallow cloned; extra row fields survive. Mapping forces api:ice-messages, provider:current ID, baseUrl:config.baseUrl. Legacy OAuth gatewayConfig is sanitized through the same path (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/radius-config.ts:7-74).

Refresh first restores stored models filtered to current provider ID through publish(update). If no stored entry and credential is OAuth, a nonempty legacy gatewayConfig catalog is published with persist.models/checkedAt and installed. Any false publish stops. Network is attempted only if allowNetwork and not aborted, using OAuth access or API-key credential.key as optional bearer; no separate generic auth derivation is invoked in this hook. GET new URL('/v1/config', gateway) sends accept:application/json plus authorization when key truthy and caller signal. Non-OK throws `Could not load Radius config from <gateway>: <status>: <trimmed body>` where body is trimmed then truncated to 512 characters plus ellipsis; invalid JSON shape throws `Invalid Radius config from <gateway>`. Signal is rechecked after fetch/config load before publishing refreshed models and checkedAt. Unlike remote builtin catalogs there is no four-hour/ETag throttle here (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/radius.ts:35-78; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/radius-config.ts:76-97).

Configured providers with oauth:"radius" and baseUrl create a Radius base using config.name??id and remove one trailing /v1 or /v1/ from gateway input. Composed models preserve gateway-provided model endpoint rather than blindly replacing it with the OAuth login gateway URL (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-runtime.ts:238-253; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:170-199).
entries.interfaces:
RadiusProviderOptions{id?, name?, gateway?}; RadiusGatewayConfig{baseUrl, models}; OAuth metadata gatewayConfig supports legacy restore. Service identity https://radius.pi.dev and OAuth client ID pi-gateway are external protocol constants, not branding strings.

`RADIUS_PROVIDER_ID` is the literal `radius`. `DEFAULT_RADIUS_GATEWAY` references `RADIUS_GATEWAY_ORIGIN`; it is not a separately computed endpoint. `RadiusGatewayModel` requires id/name, reasoning, input, cost, contextWindow and maxTokens, with optional thinkingLevelMap; `RadiusOAuthCredential` intersects OAuthCredential with optional gatewayConfig. The runtime sanitizer remains deliberately narrower than this compile-time shape, as specified above (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/radius.ts:1; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/radius-config.ts:5-25).
entries.dependency_text: AUTH-001 preserves legacy OAuth metadata, AUTH-008 applies aliases/overrides, AUTH-010 provides ModelsStore, AI-002 owns publish guards and AI-003 ice-messages protocol. Radius OAuth login is a separate flow entry.
entries.rust: The inspected native core uses compiled/manifest/local-config catalogs and has no Radius config fetch/legacy OAuth catalog conversion. Its fixed OAuth enum would discard gatewayConfig on rewrite; ModelsConfig does not represent oauth:"radius". Native Api recognizes legacy pi-messages plus arbitrary Other strings, but recognition alone does not supply a Radius gateway implementation or dynamic catalog lifecycle. External provider package contents remain unverified (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:232-273; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:359-407; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider.rs:859-920; rust:crates/ice-ai/src/types.rs:460-475).
entries.port: Implement Radius as a provider with separately owned authentication and dynamic catalog hooks, preserving legacy gatewayConfig until a durable ModelsStore publication succeeds. Add gateway alias normalization, bounded error-body reporting and exact permissive validation rules or explicitly approved stricter behavior. Maintain provider identity when adopting server models and respect publish cancellation before changing the live list.
entries.priority_reason: Radius has no static catalog fallback; losing its dynamic config or legacy metadata leaves the gateway with no selectable models.

entries.what: Provide cancellable provider-owned login interactions and reusable cryptographic/polling helpers while preserving the distinction between a generic OAuth host and an implemented provider flow.
entries.mechanism:
The authentication layer gives providers typed prompts, notifications and cancellation, with lazy loading of concrete OAuth flows. Shared helpers generate PKCE material, schedule device polling and render callback pages.

AuthPrompt is text|secret|select|manual_code with message and optional per-prompt AbortSignal; text/secret/manual may have placeholder, select has readonly id/label/description choices and resolves an ID string. AuthEvent is info(message, links?), auth_url(url, instructions?), device_code(userCode, verificationUri, intervalSeconds?, expiresInSeconds?), progress(message). The whole interaction signal is normalized before provider login. API-key auth may omit login for ambient-only readiness and may supply a side-effect-free check separately from resolve; OAuth splits login, refresh(credential, signal), toAuth(credential), allowing store-owned refresh exclusion (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/types.ts:117-237).

lazyOAuth exposes name/loginLabel without loading and caches the first loader Promise, including a rejected one. OAuth loader imports through a variable module specifier, rewriting trailing .ts→.js only when import.meta.url ends in .js, so browser bundlers do not statically chase Node callback-server modules. registerBundledOAuthFlowLoaders replaces a module-global loader set; every flow loader uses it when present, otherwise dynamic import. bun-oauth installs seven static loaders for Anthropic, Codex, Copilot, OpenRouter, Kimi, xAI, Radius; Radius gets name/gateway options (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/helpers.ts:34-54; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/load.ts:1-68; ice:packages/ai/src/bun-oauth.ts:1-22).

PKCE generates 32 cryptographically random bytes, unpadded base64url verifier, then SHA-256 of its UTF-8 string and unpadded base64url challenge. Shared device polling uses deadline Date.now()+expiresInSeconds*1000 when typeof number, otherwise Infinity; initial interval max(1000, floor((intervalSeconds??5)*1000)). Default is immediate first poll; waitBeforeFirstPoll sleeps min(interval, remaining) first. While Date.now()<deadline it checks abort, awaits poll, immediately returns complete or throws failed message. slow_down uses a finite positive server interval directly (at least 1000 ms), otherwise adds 5000 ms; it may therefore reduce a previous larger interval when the server says so. Pending/slow-down sleeps at most remaining deadline. No helper timeout races an in-flight poll and a complete result is returned before another deadline/abort check. Sleep cancellation throws Error('Login cancelled'); timeout distinguishes ordinary `Device flow timed out` from the detailed clock-drift/WSL/VM guidance after any slow_down (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/pkce.ts:1-35; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/device-code.ts:1-98).

Shared callback pages escape &,<,>, double quote, single quote for title/heading/message/details, render dark success/failure HTML and pre-wrap optional error details. They contain no automatic redirect/script. Individual flows choose status/cache headers and own server lifetime (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/oauth-page.ts:1-109). Dedicated poll tests inspect immediate/delayed first call, +5 seconds and server interval, and abortable wait; they were read, not executed (ice:packages/ai/test/oauth-device-code.test.ts:11-144).
entries.interfaces:
OAuth methods return OAuthCredential; toAuth returns ModelAuth asynchronously. Shared polling results are pending|slow_down(intervalSeconds?)|failed(message)|complete(value). Login loading, actual provider network behavior and UI display are separate boundaries.

The separate legacy extension contract is type-only: `OAuthPrompt { message: string; placeholder?: string; allowEmpty?: boolean }`; `OAuthAuthInfo { url: string; instructions?: string }`; `OAuthDeviceCodeInfo { userCode: string; verificationUri: string; intervalSeconds?: number; expiresInSeconds?: number }`; `OAuthSelectOption { id: string; label: string }`; `OAuthSelectPrompt { message: string; options: OAuthSelectOption[] }`. `OAuthLoginCallbacks` supplies onAuth/onDeviceCode void callbacks, onPrompt returning Promise<string>, optional onProgress/onManualCodeInput, required onSelect returning Promise<string | undefined>, and optional signal. These legacy declarations do not themselves perform login or polling (ice:packages/ai/src/compat/extension-oauth-types.ts:4-42).
entries.dependency_text: AUTH-001/002 define credential shape/commit; AUTH-004 automatic refresh; AI-002 normalizes interaction and owns Models login lifecycle. TUI/RPC own rendering/transport of prompt and notification variants.
entries.rust: Rust has a real native OAuth host: registered providers list non-secret manifests; request only permits begin/exchange/refresh/revoke, looks up exact provider, calls synchronous plugin callback under panic catch, frees plugin output on success/error/panic, reports nonzero status and parses returned JSON. Response version defaults 1 when absent or not u64 and otherwise must 1; kinds interaction/credential/success/error only; payload defaults null. Credential payload requires nonempty string access, defaults refresh to empty and expires_at to 0 seconds. CLI login loops interaction→plain input→exchange until credential and persists it; explicit refresh/revoke are supported. This host has no TS typed prompt variants, shared PKCE/device poller, per-step async cancellation or the seven concrete flow implementations in the audited tree. External package flows remain unverified (rust:crates/ice-extensions/src/oauth.rs:14-198; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/auth.rs:169-313).
entries.port: Retain native plugin discovery/ownership and extend its interaction protocol to represent typed prompts, cancellation and notifications. Implement reusable PKCE/polling with the source-specified timing rules, then provider-specific flows separately; do not count the generic action bridge as completed subscription support. Preserve explicit response version/credential compatibility for existing plugins while defining epoch unit conversion and missing-field errors.
entries.priority_reason: Generic OAuth registration cannot reproduce login UX, cancellation or device authorization behavior without these contracts.

entries.what: Authenticate Claude subscription users through PKCE with a local callback or pasted code, then refresh the same credential using its exact provider protocol.
entries.mechanism:
Anthropic subscription login races a browser callback against manually supplied authorization input. Both routes exchange the same PKCE authorization and store a refreshable credential with an explicit expiry margin.

Client ID is 9d1c250a-e61b-44d9-88ed-5944d1962f5e (decoded by source); authorize endpoint https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize. Token endpoint initializer is redacted in source, but visible test assertions identify https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token. Callback listens at module-load ICE_OAUTH_CALLBACK_HOST||127.0.0.1, fixed port 53692/path/callback; advertised redirect stays http://localhost:53692/callback even when bind host differs. Node http is loaded lazily through a memoized Promise, unavailable runtime throws. Callback path/state/code are validated in that order, returning 404/400/400 or 200; errors return 500. Bind failure yields a no-op server whose wait immediately returns null, enabling manual fallback (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openai-codex.ts:8-70; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openai-codex.ts:293-394).

Browser login notifies auth_url then starts manual_code prompt. Callback and manual input share one wait winner; manual errors propagate; manual input parser accepts trimmed URL, code#state, code= parameters, or bare code, with optional supplied state required to match. Missing code throws. Whole-login abort cancels callback wait; finally aborts manual prompt and closes server. There is no overall browser timeout. Every 403 or 404 is pending before body inspection, including an access_denied body. Other errors parse string error or error.code: deviceauth_authorization_pending→pending, slow_down→slow_down, else failed with status/full response body. Successful poll requires authorization_code/code_verifier, then exchanges with redirect_uri https://auth.openai.com/deviceauth/callback. It requires string device/user/verification values, optional numeric interval and numeric expires_in; verification_uri must parse with http: or https:, and normalized href is emitted. A string access_token is complete; authorization_pending waits; slow_down forwards numeric interval to the shared helper; other OAuth errors produce `Device flow failed: <error>[: <description>]`; malformed body fails. The GitHub access token is then retained in credential.refresh and used as Bearer to GET the Copilot internal token. Response requires string token/numeric expires_at; credential.access=token, expires=expires_at*1000−300000, enterpriseUrl=normalized domain/undefined (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/github-copilot.ts:134-141; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/github-copilot.ts:200-285).

Request base URL first extracts token `proxy-ep=([^;]+)` and changes leading proxy. to api.; otherwise enterprise→https://copilot-api.<domain>, otherwise https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com. toAuth returns this baseUrl and access as apiKey on every request. entries.title: OpenRouter one-shot PKCE login and permanent OAuth-minted API key
entries.what: Mint a user-controlled OpenRouter API key through browser or manual PKCE login and reuse it across text and image generation without refreshing it as an expiring token.
entries.mechanism:
OpenRouter login exchanges a one-use PKCE authorization for a permanent API key. Browser callbacks and manual input share ownership of the exchange, and the resulting credential is shared by text and image providers.

Login generates PKCE plus random callback path /oauth/callback/<UUID>, binds an ephemeral port 0 on current ICE_OAUTH_CALLBACK_HOST||127.0.0.1 and advertises that host/actual port. The authorize URL https://openrouter.ai/auth receives callback_url, code_challenge, code_challenge_method:S256; there is no separate OAuth state parameter. It emits listening progress then auth_url, then races manual_code prompt against a callback that performs the exchange itself (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openrouter.ts:20-43; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openrouter.ts:135-240; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openrouter.ts:242-298).

Callback accepts only GET with exact unpredictable path; other requests 404. claimed/settled callback 409 prevents duplicate exchanges. OAuth error 400 settles rejection; missing code 400 leaves wait open. First valid code claims exchange, success page 200 and credential settlement; exchange failure 502 and login rejection. Every page sets content-type HTML UTF-8 and cache-control:no-store. finish settles once, clears timer/listener and closes server. Initial bind errors reject; post-listen server errors settle. A 5-minute timer fails pending login. User abort rejects Login cancelled. Manual completion/error hands off only if callback has not claimed exchange; after callback result a recorded manualError still takes precedence. finally aborts the manual prompt and closes the server. Manual parser trims URL/query code or bare code, with no #state form; empty/missing code rejects (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openrouter.ts:45-67; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openrouter.ts:135-298).

Exchange POSTs JSON {code, code_verifier, code_challenge_method:S256}, JSON Accept/content-type, with a dedicated 30 s controller linked to caller; cancellation and timeout get distinct exact messages. TOKEN_URL literal is redacted both in implementation 21 and test 9, so its exact endpoint remains an evidence limitation rather than inferred from memory. Success JSON must be a nonarray object with nonempty string key; malformed successful JSON and absent key have distinct errors. Non-OK detail precedence is error_description→message→string error→nested error.message, included in `OpenRouter OAuth key exchange failed (HTTP <status>)`. Credential is type:oauth, access:key, refresh:"", expires:Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. refresh returns the same credential unchanged, ignoring its signal; toAuth returns access as apiKey (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openrouter.ts:69-133; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openrouter.ts:301-311).

Tests specify shared stored OAuth key for text/images, PKCE digest, one exchange despite duplicate callback, callback 502 plus login failure, manual URL/bare code, cancellation, no-key error and configured callback host; source was read, not run (ice:packages/ai/test/openrouter-oauth.test.ts:29-320).

entries.what: Authenticate a Kimi Code subscription through device authorization, renew credentials with its provider-specific retry rules, and send the resulting access token as an Authorization header.
entries.mechanism:

Resolve the OAuth host on each login or refresh from KIMI_CODE_OAUTH_HOST, then KIMI_OAUTH_HOST, then https://auth.kimi.com; remove trailing slashes. Client ID is 17e5f671-d194-4dfb-9706-5516cb48c098. Each device, poll and refresh fetch receives AbortSignal.any of caller signal and a fresh 30-second timeout. Device initiation POSTs form client_id to /api/oauth/device_authorization with JSON Accept; both verification URLs must parse as HTTP(S), though the original strings are retained, and device/user code need only have string type. Finite positive expires_in/interval are used; otherwise defaults 900 seconds and 5 seconds. The UI receives verification_uri_complete. Polling waits before its first request and POSTs client_id, device_code, device grant to /api/oauth/token (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/kimi-coding.ts:13-117; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/kimi-coding.ts:141-164; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/kimi-coding.ts:281-292).

Polling HTTP>=500 fails immediately with status and body. Successful access-token responses still require nonempty access and refresh tokens and finite positive expires_in. authorization_pending continues; slow_down supplies a positive numeric interval or lets the common helper add 5 seconds; expired_token and access_denied have distinct user-facing errors. Other failures include status and string error/description. Tokens expire at Date.now()+expires_in*1000 without an OAuth-flow skew (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/kimi-coding.ts:119-207).

Refresh POSTs client_id, grant_type:refresh_token, refresh_token. REFRESH_MAX_RETRIES=3 means four total attempts; later attempts sleep 1,2,4 seconds with caller cancellation. Transport exceptions retry. HTTP429 or>=500 retry while attempts remain; 401,403 or invalid_grant fail immediately with an unauthorized message; all other non-OK responses fail immediately with status and parsed JSON. Successful malformed tokens fail immediately. A canceled fetch is caught as a transport exception, but the subsequent abortable backoff/pre-attempt check terminates it. The source comment saying Models clears dead credentials is stale: this function only throws, while the authoritative resolver leaves stored credentials unchanged on refresh failure (AUTH-004; Models collection integration AI-002) (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/kimi-coding.ts:209-279).

entries.title: Radius gateway OAuth discovery, fixed callback and immediate device polling
entries.what: Support Radius browser/device login and refresh against the configured gateway while retaining the legacy pi-gateway protocol identity.
entries.mechanism:
Radius supports browser and device-code login against a configured gateway. Browser authorization uses discovery, while token exchange, device polling and refresh use fixed paths beneath that gateway.

createRadiusOAuth receives name and gateway, normalizes the gateway using the Radius helper, and exposes a browser-first select prompt with values browser and device-code (hyphenated). Client ID remains pi-gateway; scope gateway offline_access. Browser login alone GETs <gateway>/v1/oauth for authorizationEndpoint and requires only a string; URL construction happens later without the stricter verification-URL checks used by other flows. It creates PKCE and UUID state, sets response_type:code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope, code_challenge, code_challenge_method:S256, handoff:url, state, replacing any existing authorization search (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:26-67; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:221-270; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:353-389).

The browser callback is fixed http://127.0.0.1:1456/oauth/callback, with no ICE_OAUTH_CALLBACK_HOST override and no manual-code fallback. Wrong path 404, wrong state 400, provider error 400 settles null, missing code 400 leaves the wait open, valid code 200 settles. Abort settles null; binding error resolves a no-op callback server whose wait returns null. Login translates absent code to OAuth callback did not complete unless aborted, which becomes Login cancelled. Finally always closes. There is no adapter timer bounding the browser wait (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:148-219; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:221-270).

Authorization-code exchange, device polling and refresh always use <gateway>/v1/oauth/token, never a token URL from discovery. They POST form data with JSON Accept and caller signal, with no added request timeout. Non-OK errors become OAuthResponseError carrying status and OAuth error; detail comes from error/description or status, with non-JSON text accepted as description. Successful token payload is cast without the strict runtime access/refresh/lifetime checks of xAI/Kimi; stored fields are access_token, refresh_token, expiry now+expires_in*1000−60000, scope (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:69-146).

Device initiation POSTs client_id/scope to <gateway>/v1/oauth/device and checks only truthiness of device_code, user_code, verification_uri, expires_in. It does not validate their runtime types, positive finite expiry or URL scheme. Device-code UI receives the raw URI. Polling starts immediately, forwards device grant/client/device code to the direct gateway token endpoint, treats OAuthResponseError authorization_pending and slow_down specially, and emits separate expired/denied messages. Refresh uses refresh grant directly against the gateway without discovery; toAuth returns apiKey access (ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:272-351; ice:packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/radius.ts:390-403).

Source-read tests establish direct gateway endpoints for device and refresh, browser-only discovery and rejection of discovery lacking authorizationEndpoint; no requests were actually executed (ice:packages/ai/test/radius-oauth.test.ts:27-128).

entries.title: Provider attribution, session headers and caller override order
entries.what: Construct the coding-agent's provider attribution and OpenCode session headers consistently, then apply explicit caller header sources without resolving secrets.
entries.mechanism:
Provider attribution adds selected client and session headers before caller-supplied header sources. Telemetry preferences gate default attribution, while OpenCode session headers follow a separate rule.

Host classification deliberately differs by provider: OpenRouter matches provider id `openrouter` OR a case-sensitive substring `openrouter.ai` anywhere in baseUrl; NVIDIA matches id `nvidia` OR parsed hostname exactly `integrate.api.nvidia.com`; Cloudflare matches either built-in id OR hostname exactly `api.cloudflare.com`/`gateway.ai.cloudflare.com`; OpenCode matches id `opencode`/`opencode-go` OR hostname exactly `opencode.ai`. URL parse failure returns false for hostname checks (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-attribution.ts:5-34; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-attribution.ts:64-68).

A falsy sessionId suppresses session headers. Otherwise only OpenCode receives `x-opencode-session:<sessionId>` and `x-opencode-client:ice`, independently of the telemetry gate. Default attribution is wholly suppressed unless isInstallTelemetryEnabled(settingsManager) returns true. With the gate enabled, first matching branch wins: OpenRouter adds `HTTP-Referer:https://ice.dev`, `X-OpenRouter-Title:ice`, `X-OpenRouter-Categories:cli-agent`; NVIDIA adds `X-BILLING-INVOKE-ORIGIN:Ice`; Cloudflare and OpenCode each add `User-Agent:ice-coding-agent`. This helper delegates the telemetry-policy default and environment opt-outs to its dependency; it does not decide them itself (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-attribution.ts:36-83).

Merge order is session headers, default attribution, then each nonempty header source in argument order using Object.assign. Keys are case-sensitive at this stage, later exact-key values win, and null removal markers remain values. Empty result returns undefined. Thus an explicit same-case source overrides the generated value, but differently cased duplicate names can coexist until the downstream request-header merger handles them (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-attribution.ts:85-103).
entries.interfaces: mergeProviderAttributionHeaders(model, settingsManager, sessionId,...ProviderHeaders[])→ProviderHeaders|undefined. It is a synchronous, no-I/O composition helper; host matching and null values are observable at the request boundary.

entries.title: Exact references, fuzzy patterns and ordered scoped-model expansion
entries.what: Resolve saved/model-scope patterns into an ordered, deduplicated collection of model identities with optional thinking overrides and explicit diagnostics.
entries.mechanism:
Model scopes expand exact references, fuzzy patterns and globs into an ordered set of model identities. Parsing preserves literal model identifiers before interpreting thinking suffixes and returns structured diagnostics.

The exact-reference helper trims the whole reference, rejects empty, and compares case-insensitively. It first requires a unique canonical provider/id match, then permits a first-slash provider/id match with each part trimmed, then requires a unique bare id. More than one match at either canonical/provider stage immediately returns undefined. The fuzzy helper first invokes this exact helper; on failure it matches case-insensitive substrings of id or optional name, prefers aliases over dated ids, and sorts descending by id.localeCompare. An alias is any id not ending `-` plus exactly eight digits (and explicitly any `-latest` id). Consequently an ambiguous bare exact match can still be selected by fuzzy fallback, and an empty raw fuzzy pattern matches every id; the stricter exact helper's rejection is not the final fuzzy result (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-resolver.ts:72-164).

parseModelPattern first tries the entire pattern—including literal colons—through that exact/fuzzy helper. A full match returns thinkingLevel undefined, not `off` despite the nearby comment. On failure it splits at the last colon. Valid thinking suffixes recurse on the prefix; the outer suffix wins only when the inner result has no warning. Invalid suffixes use fallback by default: recurse on the prefix, return undefined thinking and `Invalid thinking level "<suffix>" in pattern "<pattern>". Using default instead.` if a model is found. With allowInvalidThinkingLevelFallback:false the invalid suffix is treated as part of an unmatched id and no warning is returned. No match/no colon returns all optional values undefined (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-resolver.ts:189-255).

Scope expansion copies the available-model list and processes patterns in caller order. A pattern containing `*`, `?` or `[` takes the glob branch. Only a valid last-colon thinking suffix is removed there; invalid suffixes remain literal glob text. An exact reference match is attempted before globbing, preserving literal bracket-containing ids. Otherwise minimatch({nocase:true}) matches canonical provider/id OR bare id and returns all matching catalog entries in catalog order. Non-glob patterns produce one fuzzy/parsed result. Both paths deduplicate using modelsAreEqual, with the first occurrence—including its thinking value—winning. A no-match produces type warning/code no-match/message `No models match pattern "<pattern>"`; invalid-thinking warnings use code invalid-thinking-level. The pure helper returns diagnostics without printing; the async wrapper obtains getAvailable(undefined, options), while resolveModelScope prints each warning in yellow and returns only the scoped models (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-resolver.ts:268-379).
entries.interfaces:
findExactModelReferenceMatch; parseModelPattern(pattern, models,{allowInvalidThinkingLevelFallback?}); resolveModelScopeFromModels→{scopedModels:[{model, thinkingLevel?}], diagnostics:[{type:"warning", code, message, pattern}]}; async resolveModelScope[WithDiagnostics]. Order and provider+model identity are part of the contract.

`ParsedModelResult` requires `model: Model<Api>|undefined` and `warning:string|undefined`, with optional thinkingLevel. `ModelScopeDiagnostic` is warning with code no-match|invalid-thinking-level plus message/pattern, and `ResolveModelScopeResult` contains scopedModels and diagnostics arrays. `resolveModelScopeWithDiagnostics` obtains available models with the supplied auth-operation options, then calls the pure expansion helper (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-resolver.ts:166-171; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-resolver.ts:268-278; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-resolver.ts:362-368).

entries.title: CLI model selection, authenticated ambiguity and custom-id fallback
entries.what: Select a model from CLI flags without requiring preexisting credentials, while disambiguating duplicate ids and retaining custom provider model identifiers.
entries.mechanism:
CLI model selection resolves against the full catalog, using authentication metadata to disambiguate some matches. It can infer a provider, apply fuzzy matching or construct a custom model from that provider’s template.

A falsy cliModel returns no model/error even if cliProvider is supplied. Selection uses all runtime models, not only authenticated ones, permitting first-time --api-key use. Empty catalog returns `No models available. Check your installation or add models to models.json.`. A lowercase provider Map is built in catalog order; later case-colliding provider ids overwrite earlier canonical values. Explicit unknown provider returns `Unknown provider "<provider>". Use --list-models to see available providers/models.`. Without an explicit provider, a recognized prefix before the FIRST slash is preferred as provider/model. Without that inference, exact bare-id OR canonical matches are collected: one wins directly; several choose the sole hasConfiguredAuth provider, otherwise error lists locale-sorted canonical matches and distinguishes no authenticated match from multiple authenticated matches (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-resolver.ts:404-502).

An explicit --provider also tolerates and strips a matching provider/ prefix from --model. The candidate list is provider-scoped when possible, then parseModelPattern runs with invalid-thinking fallback disabled, retaining full-id-before-valid-colon-suffix and fuzzy selection. If an inferred provider selects an unauthenticated model, exactly one authenticated alternative whose bare id equals the RAW full cliModel can replace it, with undefined thinking; it does not strip a thinking suffix for that branch. A successful inferred match otherwise wins. If inference found no model, the code first uses Array.find for the first raw bare/canonical full match across all models—without the earlier ambiguity check—then tries the full pattern across all models in strict suffix mode (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-resolver.ts:504-566).

If a known provider still has no match, buildFallbackModel clones that provider's configured default-id model if present, otherwise its first catalog model; only id/name are replaced. If cliThinking is absent, a valid last-colon suffix is stripped from the fallback wire id and returned as fallbackThinking. If cliThinking is present, the suffix stays in the wire id. A requested thinking value other than off forces reasoning:true on the fallback clone. The helper returns only the parsed fallbackThinking, not cliThinking, plus `Model "<id>" not found for provider "<provider>". Using custom model id.`. Without a fallback provider model it returns `Model "<display>" not found. Use --list-models to see available models.`. The helper parses but does not apply the final thinking level (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-resolver.ts:173-187; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-resolver.ts:568-604).

entries.title: Omni endpoint catalog validation, reasoning maps and route capabilities
entries.what: Convert the local Omni /models response into usable Ice model definitions, retaining endpoint capability metadata and applying the route-specific limits that the coding agent expects.
entries.mechanism:
The Omni catalog translator turns endpoint model records into usable model definitions and capability metadata. It retains valid rows despite other invalid records and applies explicit route-specific limits and protocol choices.

mapEndpointModels requires a nonempty response.data array, otherwise throws `endpoint returned no models`. It processes entries in order, keeps valid entries, remembers only the first thrown error, and throws that error only if no valid entries survive. Each id must be a nonempty string and case-sensitive unique; the id is inserted into the seen set BEFORE validating the remaining fields, so an invalid first row reserves its id and a later otherwise-valid duplicate is rejected. Context is the first positive safe integer among capabilities.contextWindow, context_length, max_input_tokens. Missing context/output produce `<id>: invalid contextWindow`/`<id>: invalid maxOutput`. entries.what: Expose a Providers settings submenu that lists runtime catalogs, lets the user refetch one provider, and reports completion without overlapping refetch operations.
entries.mechanism:
The Providers settings submenu shows catalog counts and lets a user refetch one provider. One shared admission flag prevents overlapping refetches while list and detail navigation remain available.

The extension stores the latest session_start context and registers settings group/id `providers`. Opening before a session context exists returns a Providers unavailable view with the select-cancel key returning to the caller. Otherwise summaries come from modelRegistry.getRuntime(), and refetch uses getAgentDir(), ctx.modelRegistry.refresh, runtime.getModels(id).length and the caller's signal (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice-provider-settings.ts:181-234).

The submenu shallow-copies summaries and initially shows a provider list. Each label is the provider id, not its display name; description is `<count> models · <baseUrl ?? built-in>`. Primary column min/max widths are 12/32, visible rows are min(count,10). Empty summaries show No providers configured and cancel-key handling. Selecting a row shows a read-only Models count plus Refetch catalog with currentValue run or working; Esc from detail returns to the list. Returning to the list clears selectedProviderId (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice-provider-settings.ts:22-105; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice-provider-settings.ts:107-150).

One submenu-wide refetching boolean rejects all overlapping requests, including another provider. On start it sets status key `ice-providers` to `Refetching <id>…`, rerenders detail and creates AbortSignal.timeout(15000). Success updates only that summary's count and notifies info `Refetched <id>: <count> models`; a structured error or thrown exception notifies error `Could not refetch <id>: <error>`. Finally it clears the boolean and status, and rerenders the detail only if selectedProviderId still equals the original id. Navigating away does not abort the operation. The 15-second signal is passed to onRefetch, but AUTH-032's local branch does not forward it, so this is not a universal deadline (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice-provider-settings.ts:152-178). The dedicated test source covers refetch UI state and overlap suppression; it was read, not executed (ice:packages/coding-agent/test/ice-provider-settings.test.ts:1-90).

entries.what: Provide a reusable no-network provider whose queued messages or async factories expose deterministic state transitions and production-like text/thinking/tool streaming for downstream tests.
entries.mechanism:
Faux converts queued scripted messages or asynchronous factories into assistant events without network access. Queue ownership, callback order, partial snapshots and cancellation make its behavior observable to higher-level tests.

Random ids join the prefix, current epoch milliseconds and Math.random() base-36 fractional digits with colons. Helpers create text/thinking/tool-call blocks, random tool ids unless supplied, and assistant messages with default api/provider faux, model faux-1, stopReason stop, zero usage, optional deferred/error/responseId, and timestamp option ?? Date.now(). createFauxCore defaults provider to faux and API to a fresh random id prefixed faux. An omitted OR empty model-definition array yields faux-1 / Faux Model, text+image input, reasoning:false, zero costs, context 128000, output 16384, baseUrl http://localhost:0. Custom definitions use id as missing name and the same per-field defaults. getModel() or a falsy id returns the first model; a truthy id requires exact equality (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:23-99; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:437-487; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:645-652).

setResponses shallow-copies a replacement queue, appendResponses appends, and pending count is queue length; these operations do not reset call counters, cache or deferred state. Each stream invocation synchronously shifts one step and increments callCount BEFORE queueMicrotask begins. Inside the microtask it first awaits onResponse({status:200, headers:{}}, requestModel), then checks for an empty queue/deferred submission/normal factory. A factory receives original context, stream options, mutable shared state and request model, and may return a promise. The returned message is structured-cloned, then api/provider/model are rewritten to core/request identity and usage recomputed. Empty queue yields an error-only stream `No more faux responses queued` with estimated usage; thrown/rejected factory or callback yields error-only with zero default usage. A preaborted signal does not prevent onResponse or normal factory evaluation; it is observed when streaming begins (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:107-154; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:282-291; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:489-563; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:654-672).

streamWithDeltas starts with content:[]/stopReason:pending. Preabort emits error/aborted and ends without start; otherwise start precedes each content block's start/delta*/end and the final done/error. Text/thinking append each chunk to a mutable partial block; tool-call arguments remain {} throughout deltas and become the full object only at toolcall_end. Partial event messages are shallow copies, so previously delivered partial blocks can share later-mutated objects. StopReason pending throws `Faux response ended without a stop reason`; error/aborted terminal messages use error events, other terminal reasons use done. Abort uses `Request was aborted`, preserves accumulated partial content and refreshes timestamp. Signal checks occur before each block and AFTER waiting for each chunk, not during the timer (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:308-435).

Default chunk sizes are 3–5 tokens, each token represented by 4 JS UTF-16 code units. min is at least 1 and the minimum of configured/default min and max; max is at least min. Random size is inclusive of both endpoints, and empty text still emits one empty delta. Missing/nonpositive pacing schedules a microtask; positive pacing waits estimateTokens(chunk)/tokensPerSecond*1000. The core initializer assigning tokensPerSecond at line 446 is connector-redacted; scheduler semantics and the pacing test fixtures are visible, but the exact initializer is not asserted here (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:270-280; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:331-337; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:437-446; ice:packages/ai/test/faux-provider.test.ts:406-434; ice:packages/ai/test/faux-provider.test.ts:506-630).

FauxResponseStep=AssistantMessage|async-capable factory(context, options, state, model); createFauxCore and fauxProvider expose models/getModel/state/setResponses/appendResponses/getPendingResponseCount plus stream/streamSimple. The explicit Models collection wrapper resolves auth to an empty object and advertises both deferred methods. Legacy registration/unregister dispatch belongs AI-003.

`FauxContentBlock` is TextContent|ThinkingContent|ToolCall. `FauxProviderState` has callCount/deferredFetchCount and cancelledDeferred handles. `RegisterFauxProviderOptions` optionally supplies api/provider/model definitions, deferred pendingFetches/pollAfterMs, tokensPerSecond and tokenSize min/max. `FauxProviderRegistration` returns api, a nonempty model tuple, getModel overloads, state, response queue setters/count and unregister; `FauxProviderHandle` returns the same handle without unregister and adds provider. The factory receives context, optional SimpleStreamOptions, state and model and returns an assistant message or promise (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:40-67; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:101-154).

This entry compares Faux behavior rather than using Faux tests as evidence that unrelated production APIs pass.
entries.rust: The genuine native Faux provider already supports text/thinking/tool-call builders, a mutex-protected replace/append queue, context factories, custom model sets, default faux-1/128000/16384 metadata, paced block events, caller cancellation, and an additional abort_after test knob (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/faux.rs:23-389; rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/faux.rs:478-569; rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/faux.rs:678-885; rust:crates/ice-ai/tests/faux.rs:40-223). Empty native queue proceeds through normal streamWithDeltas, so it includes start before error; TS empty-queue handling is error-only. Native message/event clones retain independent partial content, and chunking respects Unicode boundaries rather than slicing UTF-16 units. These are concrete differences within an existing provider, not a missing Faux implementation (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/faux.rs:87-96; rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/faux.rs:192-226; rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/faux.rs:328-389; rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/faux.rs:478-550; rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/faux.rs:678-928).

Preserve native Unicode-safe chunks and independent snapshots unless strict mutation compatibility is explicitly needed; record these as intentional safer deviations. Resolve the redacted pacing initializer before certifying option normalization. Use existing TS/native test sources to derive fixtures without claiming this audit ran them.

entries.title: Faux usage serialization and prompt-cache affinity
entries.what: Estimate Faux token usage from a specified serialized prompt and simulate shared-prefix cache accounting per session or explicit prompt-cache key.
entries.mechanism:
Faux estimates usage from a defined serialization of the prompt and assistant output. A per-core cache tracks common prompt prefixes under a session or explicit cache key.

estimateTokens is ceil(JS string.length/4), counting UTF-16 code units. User content is raw text or newline-joined text/image blocks; images serialize as `[image:<mimeType>:<data.length>]`. Assistant content joins text, thinking or `<toolName>:<JSON.stringify(arguments)>` by newline. Tool results join toolName and each text/image block by newline. serializeContext emits a system segment only for truthy systemPrompt, then `<role>:<serialized message>` for every message, then `tools:<JSON.stringify(tools)>` only for a nonempty tool list; segments join with two newlines. Output tokens use serialized assistant content. Scripted usage is always replaced by this estimate (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:156-218; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:229-268; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:489-501).

The cache key is options.promptCacheKey ?? options.sessionId; a defined empty promptCacheKey suppresses fallback to sessionId and disables caching because the selected key is falsy. Caching is enabled for a truthy key unless cacheRetention is exactly none. Each core owns a Map of previous serialized prompts. If the previous prompt is truthy, commonPrefixLength compares UTF-16 units, cacheRead=ceil(prefix.length/4), cacheWrite=ceil(newSuffix.length/4), input=max(0, promptTokens-cacheRead). Otherwise cacheWrite=promptTokens and input remains promptTokens. The new prompt is stored after accounting. Consequently the first cached request counts prompt tokens in both input and cacheWrite, and totalTokens is the sum of input, output, cacheRead and cacheWrite. All monetary cost fields are zero. cacheRetention:none performs no read or update and does not erase a prior cache entry; queue replacement also leaves the cache intact (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:220-268; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:437-461; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:664-666).

Different session ids have distinct cache entries; an explicit shared promptCacheKey shares affinity without changing session identity. Tests assert isolated sessions, prefix reuse, explicit shared keys and none behavior (ice:packages/ai/test/faux-provider.test.ts:214-369). These are fixture semantics, not a claim to match a real provider's tokenizer or billing.
entries.interfaces: Internal withUsageEstimate(message, context, options, promptCache) rewrites usage {input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, totalTokens, cost}; cache state is per createFauxCore and has no public clear method.
entries.dependency_text: AUTH-029 determines which normal/error/deferred responses invoke the estimator; AI-006 owns request cacheRetention/sessionId/promptCacheKey fields. Session-level cache-key propagation has separate ownership.
entries.rust: Native Faux always computes a cold estimate with ceil(UTF-8 byte length/4), input=prompt tokens, cache_read/cache_write=0 and total=input+output. Its serialization includes Some(empty) system prompts, omits tools entirely, writes tool results as `toolResult:<name>:<text>` and ignores nontext tool-result blocks. It already emits zero-cost usage and handles user image placeholders, so only the serialization/counting/cache behavior is incomplete (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/faux.rs:175-186; rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/faux.rs:575-674). The native test checks positive estimated input but does not establish TS cache-affinity equivalence (rust:crates/ice-ai/tests/faux.rs:40-78).
entries.port: Add a per-provider prompt-cache store and reproduce the serialized prompt, UTF-16 counting and exact first/repeat accounting if TS fixture compatibility is desired. Keep cache key and session identity separate, retain cache through queue replacement, and make none skip updates. If the native estimator intentionally retains UTF-8 accounting, document that deviation and use parity fixtures that expose multibyte text, tool schemas, image tool results, empty prompts and prefix-rounding effects rather than comparing only positive token counts.
entries.priority_reason: Cache/token assertions and compaction-threshold tests can differ despite identical scripted messages.

entries.title: Faux deferred submission, per-handle polling and cancellation
entries.what: Allow a Faux request to defer factory execution, return a reusable typed handle, poll until ready, cache its final answer and record cancellation independently for each submitted response.
entries.mechanism:
Faux can reserve a queued response at submission and evaluate it later through a deferred handle. Each handle tracks pending polls, a cached final answer and cancellation state.

A truthy streamOptions.deferred still shifts a queue step and increments callCount at submission, but does not evaluate it. After onResponse it creates a random deferred id and handle {provider:requestModel.provider, modelId:requestModel.id, api:requestModel.api, id, pollAfterMs?}; pollAfterMs is copied whenever not undefined, without numeric validation here. The entry stores original step/context/options/model references, pendingFetches=max(0, floor(configured??0)), cancelled:false and no final answer. It streams an empty, zero-usage deferred message through start+done; a preaborted signal is checked only inside streaming, after the handle entry has been created (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:294-306; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:437-461; ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:504-550).

Every fetch increments deferredFetchCount before its microtask and awaits fetchOptions.onResponse({status:200, headers:{}}, requestModel) before lookup. A valid lookup requires handle id and matching stored handle provider/modelId/api; it does not separately require requestModel to match those fields. Unknown handles error `Unknown faux deferred response: <id>`, cancelled entries error `Faux deferred response was cancelled: <id>`. Positive pendingFetches is decremented before streaming another empty deferred message with the original handle and requestModel message identity. It remains decremented even if the fetch signal then aborts (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:568-601).

When ready, a missing final answer triggers resolveResponse using the original step/context/model and original submission options EXCEPT deferred, signal and onResponse, which are stripped. Factory errors become a cached error message. The final result is stored indefinitely and subsequent fetches stream it again, applying the current fetch signal only during deltas. There is no stored in-flight promise: concurrent ready fetches can both observe !entry.final and evaluate an async factory before either stores a result. A preaborted fetch can likewise evaluate/cache the factory before streamWithDeltas observes abort. Entries are not deleted after ready or cancellation (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:603-629).

cancelDeferred immediately appends a structured clone of the supplied handle to cancelledDeferred, looks up by id ONLY and marks an existing entry cancelled, then awaits cancelOptions.onResponse({status:200, headers:{}}, requestModel). Unknown ids succeed and are still recorded; mismatching provider/model/api do not block id-based cancellation; cancelOptions.signal is unused. If onResponse throws, cancellation/recording have already happened. Tests source asserts submit→pending→ready count/state and in-band factory failure/cancelled fetch error (ice:packages/ai/src/providers/faux.ts:634-643; ice:packages/ai/test/providers.test.ts:574-627).
entries.interfaces: fetchDeferred(requestModel, handle, options?)→AssistantMessageEventStream; cancelDeferred(requestModel, handle, options?)→Promise<void>; state {callCount, deferredFetchCount, cancelledDeferred}. Handle identity, stored options and submission/fetch cancellation boundaries are observable.

General agent/harness deferred resume is a separate capability and must not be inferred from this test provider alone.

Native Faux DOES advertise DeferredProvider and implements stream_deferred using a global FIFO of DeferredPoll::Message/StillDeferred/Error, with push_deferred_poll as a script surface (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/faux.rs:334-469). It removes one global poll item regardless of handle, ignores model/options parameters, emits start with a default Faux placeholder and then a terminal event, clears deferred from ready messages, and reports an empty queue as error content mentioning handle.id. There is no per-handle submission registry, pending counter, deferred factory storage/final cache, fetch count or cancellation list in the native Faux struct. No Faux-specific cancel override implements the TS cancellation lifecycle. Native scripted deferred support must be retained rather than replaced with a claim of absence (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/faux.rs:328-469; rust:crates/ice-ai/src/providers/faux.rs:478-550).

entries.title: Omni catalog refresh, auth bootstrap and local versus remote refetch
entries.what: Refresh and persist the local Omni provider's catalog on demand, expose provider summaries, and distinguish this local file update from a normal runtime network refresh.
entries.mechanism:
Explicit Omni refetch writes a translated local catalog and then refreshes the runtime from disk. Startup only bootstraps the local key, while ordinary nonlocal refetch follows a separate network-refresh path.

Provider id is omni. Base URL uses nullish precedence ICE_OMNI_BASE_URL, ICE_LOCAL_BASE_URL, config.providers.omni.baseUrl, then http://127.0.0.1:20128/v1; empty strings are not skipped. loadLocalApiKey reads raw agentDir/auth.json, JSON.parse, then auth.omni?.key ?? auth.local?.key; a falsy result throws `missing omni API key in <authPath>`. It does not inspect credential type, acquire AuthStorage locks, evaluate credential expressions or use OAuth resolution (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice-provider.ts:10-17; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice-provider.ts:42-71).

refreshLocalModels catches its entire operation and returns {updated:false, error} rather than throwing. It loads the key first, then models.json (ENOENT means {}; other read/parse failures stop). It fetches `${baseUrl}/models` without slash normalization, with Authorization Bearer rawKey and an independent 30000 ms AbortSignal.timeout. Non-OK yields `model endpoint returned HTTP <status>`. AUTH-027 maps the JSON. The existing config object preserves unrelated properties/providers, but providers.omni is REPLACED with {baseUrl, api:"openai-completions", apiKey, authHeader:true, models}, and providers.local is deleted. It sets process.env.ICE_LOCAL_API_KEY BEFORE persistence, writes pretty JSON plus newline to sibling `.models.json.ice-<pid>` with mode 0600, then renames over models.json. There is no explicit file lock, random/exclusive temp name, fsync, cleanup on error or environment rollback in this function. Success returns {updated:true, count:models.length} (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice-provider.ts:252-290).

refreshLocalModelsForStartup merely tries to load the raw key into ICE_LOCAL_API_KEY and swallows errors. Its skip, refresh and onFailure options are unused; it never fetches or rewrites models.json, including when no catalog is present (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice-provider.ts:292-303). summarizeProviderCatalogs preserves runtime provider order and returns id, name??id, per-provider modelCount, plus baseUrl only if truthy (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice-provider.ts:305-315).

refetchProviderCatalog uses isLocalProvider override when supplied, otherwise providerId===omni. Local branch awaits refreshLocal(agentDir); failed write returns written.error ?? `unknown error` without a runtime refresh. Successful write calls refreshRuntime({providers:[id], allowNetwork:false}) and DOES NOT forward options.signal to either operation. A runtime aborted flag returns error `timed out`; otherwise the first Map error message wins; success count is written.count??0. Nonlocal branch calls refreshRuntime({providers:[id], allowNetwork:true, force:true, signal}), maps aborted/first error the same way, and gets count from countModels?.(id)??0. Thrown runtime errors propagate from this helper. A falsy first error message is not returned as an error by the caller's truthiness test (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice-provider.ts:317-359).
entries.interfaces: refreshLocalModels(agentDir)→LocalModelsRefreshResult; refreshLocalModelsForStartup(agentDir, options)→void; summarizeProviderCatalogs; refetchProviderCatalog→{ok:true, providerId, count}|{ok:false, providerId, error}. Explicit refetch, runtime refresh and startup bootstrap are different operations.

entries.source:
ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-config.ts:10-127; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-config.ts:144-198; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:81-129; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/model-registry.test.ts:601-975. Public runtime-only declaration distinction: ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:561-564 and ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:636-640.

Exported symbols: `ChatTemplateKwargValue`, `OpenAIResponsesCompat`, `AnthropicMessagesCompat`, `BedrockCompat`, `OpenRouterRouting`, `VercelGatewayRouting` (ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:83; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:625; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:643; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:699; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:710; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:784).
entries.what: Accept and retain the exact nested compatibility metadata that custom providers and model overrides use to select request formats, routing and tool/cache capabilities.
entries.mechanism:
Compatibility metadata controls provider request formats, routing, caching and tool capabilities. Configuration accepts optional object unions and later merges selected nested objects, with weaker validation boundaries than a closed per-protocol schema.

Provider-level compat, models[].compat and modelOverrides[id].compat all use the same Type.Union of OpenAICompletionsCompatSchema, OpenAIResponsesCompatSchema and AnthropicMessagesCompatSchema. Each declared member is optional. These are schema declarations without an API discriminator or requested additionalProperties:false; do not interpret them as a closed unknown-field rejection contract. Parsing validates the complete models.json before publishing any provider (AUTH-007). This entry specifies configuration types; defaults and request-body consequences remain owned by the corresponding AI protocol entries (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-config.ts:73-127; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-config.ts:144-198).

Completions optional booleans: supportsStore, supportsDeveloperRole, supportsReasoningEffort, thinkingCanDisable, supportsUsageInStreaming, requiresToolResultName, requiresAssistantAfterToolResult, requiresThinkingAsText, requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages, supportsOpenAIGrammarTools, supportsStrictMode, sendSessionAffinityHeaders, supportsLongCacheRetention. Other Completions fields: maxTokensField is `max_completion_tokens` or `max_tokens`; thinkingFormat is string; cacheControlFormat is literal `anthropic`; deferredToolsMode is literal `kimi`; sessionAffinityFormat is `openai`, `openai-nosession` or `openrouter`; chatTemplateKwargs and chatTemplateArgs are maps of the value union below; openRouterRouting and vercelGatewayRouting use their nested schemas (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-config.ts:66-98).

A chat-template map value may be string, number, boolean, null OR an object with required `$var` exactly `thinking.enabled` or `thinking.effort`, plus optional omitWhenOff:boolean. Responses optional booleans are supportsDeveloperRole, supportsLongCacheRetention, supportsStrictMode, supportsOpenAIGrammarTools and supportsToolSearch; its sessionAffinityFormat has the same three literals. Anthropic optional booleans are supportsEagerToolInputStreaming, supportsLongCacheRetention, sendSessionAffinityHeaders, supportsCacheControlOnTools, supportsTemperature, forceAdaptiveThinking, allowEmptySignature, supportsStrictTools and supportsToolReferences (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-config.ts:66-71; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-config.ts:100-121).

OpenRouter routing optional fields: allow_fallbacks:boolean; require_parameters:boolean; data_collection:`deny`|`allow`; zdr:boolean; enforce_distillable_text:boolean; order/only/ignore/quantizations:string[]; sort:string OR {by?:string, partition?:string|null}; max_price:{prompt?, completion?, image?, audio?, request?}, each number|string; preferred_min_throughput and preferred_max_latency each number OR {p50?, p75?, p90?, p99?}, each percentile value number. Vercel routing has only?:string[] and order?:string[]. These declarations impose no positivity, percentage bounds or nonempty-array/string constraint beyond the explicitly stated shape (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-config.ts:10-52).

Composition merges compat top-level keys and, specifically, one additional object level for openRouterRouting, vercelGatewayRouting, chatTemplateKwargs and chatTemplateArgs. It does not recursively merge grandchildren; arrays replace, so a later routing object’s arrays or nested max_price/sort object replace the earlier value at that inner key. AUTH-008 gives the provider/model/extension layer order. Existing model-registry test source covers routing, chat-template and overrides; it does not establish live remote-provider acceptance (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/provider-composer.ts:81-129; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/model-registry.test.ts:601-975).

These field lists describe individual union arms, not a universal closed validation boundary. Because all three arms are optional-field objects that permit undeclared properties, a value with a wrong type in a field unique to one arm can satisfy another arm that treats it as undeclared; for example, the Responses arm does not constrain supportsStore. This is a source-derived consequence of the schema structure, not an executed validation result. The TS public runtime additionally declares Completions supportsFinishReason and Responses supportsExplicitPromptCacheMode, omitted from these config-schema declarations; their absence from the declaration is not proof they are rejected or stripped from an accepted object (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-config.ts:73-127; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:561-564; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:636-640).
entries.interfaces:
models.json paths: providers.<id>.compat; providers.<id>.models[].compat; providers.<id>.modelOverrides.<modelId>.compat. All fields are optional except `$var` when the object arm of a chat-template value is used. No credential expression runs during schema validation.

The public runtime type names are `ChatTemplateKwargValue`, `OpenAIResponsesCompat`, `AnthropicMessagesCompat`, `BedrockCompat`, `OpenRouterRouting`, and `VercelGatewayRouting`. The Bedrock runtime record has only optional `supportsStrictMode?: boolean`; it is not a separately tagged arm of the models.json compatibility union. The other runtime-only declaration differences, including supportsExplicitPromptCacheMode, remain as documented above (ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:83-91; ice:packages/ai/src/types.ts:625-789).
entries.dependency_text: AUTH-007 handles whole-file validation/errors and AUTH-008 layer precedence. AI-005 owns thinking-level behavior; AI-003 dispatch, AI-006 common options and later protocol-specific AI entries own request option/capability effects. This is model/provider configuration, not the model-facing tool schema compiler owned by AI-012.
entries.rust:
Native has real typed Anthropic/OpenAI compatibility structs and an opaque Other carrier; these must be preserved. Anthropic already declares all nine optional fields above. Native Completions declares supportsStore, supportsDeveloperRole, supportsReasoningEffort, supportsUsageInStreaming, supportsFinishReason (also present in the TS public runtime type but omitted from this TS config-schema declaration), maxTokensField, requiresToolResultName, requiresAssistantAfterToolResult, requiresThinkingAsText, requiresReasoningContent, supportsStrictMode, sendSessionAffinityHeaders and supportsLongCacheRetention. The shorter requiresReasoningContent JSON name differs from TS requiresReasoningContentOnAssistantMessages. It lacks the remaining TS routing/chat-template/thinking-format/affinity/grammar fields. Native Responses supports the four booleans supportsDeveloperRole, supportsLongCacheRetention, supportsStrictMode, supportsOpenAIGrammarTools but not sessionAffinityFormat or supportsToolSearch (rust:crates/ice-ai/src/model.rs:10-64; rust:crates/ice-ai/src/model.rs:94-157).

Rust models.json ProviderConfig has no provider compat or modelOverrides carrier. ModelDefinition.compat is an optional raw JSON Value. Its conversion decodes this value only for native OpenAI Completions/Responses, silently leaves compat unset on serde failure, and does not apply Anthropic def.compat in that helper; unknown struct fields are not requested to be denied. This is the actual conversion called by CLI catalog assembly, not an unused comment-only path (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:359-405; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:917-927; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/provider.rs:885-901). Thus matching native struct fields do not by themselves prove configuration reachability or TS merge behavior.
entries.port: Extend the native config carriers and compatibility structs with explicit serde names/types for every field above, including nested routing and chat-template values, and carry provider/model/override layers through AUTH-008. Ensure the Anthropic config path actually applies its already-existing compat struct. Make compatibility decode errors and unknown-field handling consistent with the chosen TS schema policy instead of silently dropping the entire compat blob. Retain supportsFinishReason and opaque custom compat. supportsFinishReason is not a Rust-only runtime feature: TS declares and consumes it even though this config-schema arm omits its declaration. Request encoding changes stay in the AI protocol implementations.
entries.priority_reason: Custom model configuration currently drops capability and routing controls even for implemented wire protocols.
